purpose: Keep the ordered unqualified join view separate from each visible relation qualifier.

anchor: Binder(const SqlSyntax& syntax, const Catalog& catalog, const BindOptions& options)

purpose: Bound and restore active recursive binding depth with RAII.
inputs_outputs: Construction borrows Binder, rejects depth >= recursion_limit, then increments depth; destruction decrements it. Copy/assignment are deleted.
invariants: Only successfully constructed frames decrement, including exception unwinding. select, from and bind_expression share the same active-depth counter; this measures nested binder calls rather than raw JSON depth.
ownership: Nonowning Binder reference is valid for the frame's lexical lifetime; no heap storage or transferred ownership.
failure: Construction throws Failure(resource_limit) before increment on exhaustion. Destructor only decrements and introduces no failure path.
cost: Constant work and stack-sized state per active call; O(active depth) frame memory overall.

purpose: Count selected binder work checkpoints without allowing counter wrap or a configured threshold overrun.
inputs_outputs: Reads result_.limits.work_limit and result_.work; increments exactly once on success.
invariants: Configured zero rejects the first charge; absent configured bound still rejects uint64 maximum. Checks precede increment. It does not account for every loop, metadata validation, string/container operation or byte allocation.
ownership: Mutates only the private result work counter.
failure: Throws Failure(resource_limit) with no location before modifying work on overflow/limit exhaustion; partial result is discarded by the public boundary.
cost: Constant work and no successful-path allocation; error construction/unwinding may allocate.
review_author: Codex binding source reviewer (inspection-v4-binding-v1)

purpose: Read an optional AST byte location and reject offsets beyond the owned SQL source.
inputs_outputs: Nonobjects, omitted location or negative int64 location yield no location; an in-range nonnegative location becomes size_t, including source.size().

anchor: void keys(const Json& node, std::initializer_list<std::string_view> allowed) {

inputs_outputs: Charges one work step, requires an object, then checks each key against the supplied fixed allowlist.

anchor: const Json& tagged(const Json& node, std::string_view name) const {

inputs_outputs: Accepts an object with exactly one field equal to name and object-valued content; returns node.at(name).

ownership: Returns a const reference into the supplied AST; it is valid only while that JSON subtree remains alive and unchanged.

cost: Fixed number of JSON object checks/lookups, logarithmic in field count; no success-path payload copy.

purpose: Extract the parser-folded or quoted identifier text from a String wrapper.
inputs_outputs: Calls tagged(node,"String") and returns its string sval, defaulting to an empty string when the field is absent.
invariants: Does not perform case folding, schema lookup, key validation or nonempty-name checks; PostgreSQL parsing and the consuming context supply those rules.

anchor: ExpressionId append(SqlType type, BoundNode node, std::optional<std::size_t> where) {
purpose: Append one fully owned expression and assign its dense result-local ID.
inputs_outputs: Charges work, rejects expressions.size() >= expression_limit, then pushes type, moved node and location and returns the former size.

ownership: Takes node by value and moves it into result_.expressions; caller argument construction/copying may occur before the check.
failure: Throws Failure(resource_limit) at either checked bound; vector/payload allocation failures unwind to bind_sql. No partially built result is exposed.
cost: Amortized constant vector insertion in element count, with potentially linear payload copies/moves on capacity growth; owns the new literal bytes or argument vector and may allocate.

purpose: Borrow an existing private result expression by its trusted local ID.
inputs_outputs: Returns result_.expressions[id.value] using unchecked vector subscripting.
invariants: Caller must supply an in-range ID from this Binder. The reference must not be retained across append/operation that can grow the expression vector.
ownership: Returns a nonowning const reference; the Binder owns the expression and may relocate it.
failure: No diagnostic or bounds check; invalid IDs violate the helper precondition and can cause undefined behavior.
cost: Constant indexed access, no allocation, no work charge.

anchor: ExpressionId operation(SqlOperator op, std::vector<ExpressionId> arguments, SqlType type, std::optional<std::size_t> where) {
purpose: Append an operation node with an already determined SQL result type and argument list.
inputs_outputs: Takes operator, owned argument vector, type and location; moves arguments into BoundOperation and delegates to append.
invariants: Does not infer type or check operator arity; comparison/Boolean/cast/join callers establish these. Child IDs precede the appended operation in generated bindings.

purpose: Resolve an unknown literal to an allowed contextual type in place.

purpose: Require a Boolean expression for WHERE, ON or Boolean operators/tests.

invariants: NULL may become Boolean NULL; a non-NULL untyped string is rejected by resolve_unknown rather than truth-parsed. Existing nullable Boolean expressions remain nullable.
ownership: Mutates an unknown literal's type through resolve_unknown and returns its value ID; no new node or borrowed reference escapes.

cost: Constant checks and no success allocation or added work charge.
review_author: Codex binding source reviewer (inspection-v4-binding-v1)

anchor: void comparable(ExpressionId& left, ExpressionId& right, std::optional<std::size_t> where) {
purpose: Resolve comparison operand kinds and make permitted integer width promotion explicit.
inputs_outputs: Takes operand IDs by reference; resolves unknowns against their counterpart (both unknown become string) and may replace one int32 ID with an appended widen_integer ID.
invariants: Only int32-to-int64 widening is implicit. Different noninteger kinds reject. Equal decimal kinds may carry different fixed specs without a cast; NULL resolution inherits the counterpart type. Operand nullability is retained.

cost: Constant checks plus at most one widening append/vector allocation; diagnostic kind-name/message construction allocates only on mismatch.

anchor: ExpressionId comparison(SqlOperator op, ExpressionId left, ExpressionId right, std::optional<std::size_t> where) {
purpose: Append a nullable SQL Boolean comparison after compatible operand resolution.
inputs_outputs: Copies operand IDs, invokes comparable, ORs their nullable flags and emits op(left,right) with Boolean SqlType.
invariants: Caller supplies a comparison tag; this helper does not validate the tag. NULL-capable operands produce nullable comparison type; no Boolean value evaluation or equality-class merging occurs here.
ownership: Owns the appended two-ID argument vector in the result; operands remain result-local IDs.
failure: Compatibility errors and append resource/allocation failures propagate to the public binding boundary.
cost: Constant compatibility/type work plus optional widening and one comparison append; typically one or two small argument-vector allocations and possible expression-vector growth.

purpose: Bind the supported PostgreSQL A_Const payloads into exact scalar or SQL-NULL expressions.
inputs_outputs: Checks allowed fields; handles NULL, integer payloads, textual numeric payloads, strings and booleans. Integers are classified int32/int64; strings start unknown and NULL starts unknown/nullable.
invariants: Textual numeric input first attempts complete int64 parsing; a failed token without .eE is rejected as outside int64 rather than silently becoming decimal. Other numeric text goes to exact Decimal::parse, which rejects exponent and missing-side decimal notation. No floating point conversion is used.
ownership: New literal expression owns copied string/Decimal payloads; JSON is borrowed. Decimal errors are translated to Failure at the literal location.
failure: Unsupported shapes yield unsupported_literal, oversized integer text unsupported_type, scalar parsing retains invalid_scalar/scalar_overflow. JSON errors and allocation failures reach the public catch boundary; the local Error catch preserves scalar code/message/location.

purpose: Recognize the bounded explicit cast type names and optional exact decimal precision/scale.
inputs_outputs: Accepts an unqualified name or pg_catalog.name for int8/bigint, int4/integer, text, bool/boolean, date, numeric/decimal; returns SqlType, optionally with decimal(p[,s]).
invariants: Only decimal accepts one or two literal integer typmods, with 1<=p<=38 and 0<=s<=p; omitted scale is zero. typemod is allowed in the AST key set but not interpreted. Nullability is set later from the argument.
ownership: Borrows AST, copies identifier strings and returns inline type metadata.
failure: Unsupported name/qualification/decimal range yields unsupported_type; bad modifier form yields unsupported_cast; missing/wrong JSON shape can yield invalid_ast through Json::exception.
cost: A bounded number of name/modifier checks and JSON lookups plus O(type-name bytes) copies; no scan of catalog or source data.
review_author: Codex binding source reviewer (inspection-v4-binding-v1)

anchor: ExpressionId cast(const Json& node, const Scope& scope) {
purpose: Bind explicit literal validation or a full-type identity cast without erasing the cast node.
inputs_outputs: Resolves target type before binding the argument, inherits its nullability, mutates a literal payload/type when exactly representable, then appends literal_cast; nonliteral arguments require equal SqlType and append identity_cast.
invariants: String-to-text/date/decimal/int32/int64 and integer-to-integer exact casts are supported, plus same-kind bool/date/decimal literals and NULL to a supported target. String-to-Boolean, integer-to-decimal/text and representation-changing nonliteral casts reject. Fixed decimal casts must fit without rounding; an already-cast expression is nonliteral for further conversions.
ownership: Borrows scope/AST; copies the original literal Value before conversion, replaces the result-owned literal, then owns one cast argument vector. The reference to the literal is not used after the final append.
failure: unsupported_cast classifies unsupported/inexact conversions; Date/Decimal/catalog Error codes are retained at cast/type location by the local catch. JSON, work/expression and allocation failures propagate; private literal mutation is never returned on failure.
cost: Recursive argument-binding cost plus O(literal text bytes) copying/parsing and decimal fit formatting, then one operation append; can allocate multiple copies of a string/Decimal and a small argument vector.

anchor: ExpressionId lookup(const Scope& scope, std::optional<std::string> qualifier, const std::string& name, std::optional<std::size_t> where) {
purpose: Resolve exactly one visible column and produce candidate-specific unknown/ambiguity diagnostics.
inputs_outputs: Selects a qualifier vector or the ordered unqualified columns, scans for name matches and returns the existing defining expression ID.
invariants: Qualified lookup never falls back to unqualified names. A second matching entry is ambiguous even if its expression ID matches. For unqualified first matches, candidate description eagerly scans qualifier views; a merged key with no qualifying view is described as a merged JOIN column.
ownership: Borrows Scope and name; owns local diagnostic candidate strings and any optional qualifier copy, returning only a value ID.
failure: Reports unknown_qualifier, unknown_column or ambiguous_column at the supplied offset. Scanned entries and diagnostic candidate entries charge work and may cause resource_limit before the name diagnostic.

anchor: ExpressionId bind_expression(const Json& node, const Scope& scope) {
purpose: Recursively bind the finite scalar/Boolean SQL expression subset into typed topological nodes.
inputs_outputs: Handles one-tag ColumnRef, A_Const, ParamRef, TypeCast, binary scalar A_Expr comparisons, AND/OR/NOT, scalar NullTest and BooleanTest. Returns a new or delegated expression ID.
invariants: Only column or alias.column references are allowed; wildcards are target-only. Supported comparisons are =, <>, !=, <, <=, >, >=, optionally pg_catalog-qualified. Parameters require declared types. AND/OR require nonempty arguments; NOT requires one. NULL/Boolean IS tests produce non-null Boolean type; Boolean operands use nullable SQL typing.
ownership: Borrows AST/scope, creates result-owned nodes/vectors and copies a selected column definition for use-site location. Fixed operator recognition stores only an enum and short-lived extracted name; no lookup-map nodes are constructed.
failure: Unknown expression/operator/qualification, missing parameter, wrong Boolean type, row NULL test and bad arity reject explicitly. Scalar operator recognition precedes child binding; BooleanTest binds and checks its Boolean argument before extracting/selecting the truth test. Frame/charge/append can stop resources; malformed JSON is translated by the public boundary.
cost: Recursive AST traversal plus scope lookup/cast/literal costs, O(arity) argument vectors and O(active depth) stack. Scalar and Boolean-test spellings use fixed short branch chains without per-expression lookup-map construction; real AST/container/payload allocations remain.

anchor: Scope Binder::merge(Scope left, Scope right, std::optional<std::size_t> where) {
purpose: Combine disjoint visible relation qualifiers and concatenate ordered unqualified columns.
inputs_outputs: Takes two scopes by value, inserts every right qualifier into left with one charge each, copies right columns after left columns, and returns the combined scope.
invariants: Duplicate qualifier names fail rather than overwrite; duplicate column names remain visible for later ambiguity checks. It does not merge USING columns or expose preceding comma inputs inside a separately built ON scope.
ownership: Owns incoming scope values, moves qualifier vectors, copies qualifier keys/right column entries and returns the resulting owning scope. Lvalue callers copy complete input scopes before entering.
failure: Duplicate qualifier yields duplicate_alias at supplied location, possibly after earlier private insertions. charge/container allocation failures abort the enclosing binding; no shared caller state is mutated.

anchor: Scope Binder::alias_scope(Scope scope, const Json& alias, std::optional<std::size_t> where) {
purpose: Replace a relation or whole joined-table qualifier view and optionally rename an ordered column prefix.
inputs_outputs: Consumes a scope, validates aliasname/colnames, rewrites at most the first columns.size() names and replaces all qualifier views with one alias-to-column copy.
invariants: Alias must be nonempty; a rename list cannot exceed input arity, but duplicate visible column names are retained. A whole-join alias hides underlying relation qualifiers; physical expression IDs are unchanged.
ownership: Owns the input scope, copies alias and optional renamed strings, clears old qualifier vectors and creates one owning copy of the visible columns.
failure: Empty alias yields invalid_ast; excess names alias_column_count; JSON/identifier, work and allocation failures propagate. Prefix renames are private until success.
cost: O(renamed prefix + old qualifier storage destruction + all visible column-name bytes) work/copy and one map/vector view allocation; per-name charges do not cover the final whole-view copy.

purpose: Build physical occurrences and SQL-visible scopes for relations and INNER/CROSS/USING/NATURAL joins.
inputs_outputs: RangeVar resolves a flat catalog table and emits an occurrence plus one canonical BoundColumn per physical column. JoinExpr recursively binds two inputs, retains predicates and returns their merged or aliased visible scope.
invariants: Schema/catalog-qualified tables and non-INNER joins reject. Each base reference is distinct and keeps inh intent. NATURAL discovers unique common names in left-input order; USING preserves listed order, emits equalities and non-null left using_value outputs, then remaining left/right columns. Qualified inputs remain physical. ON sees only its join inputs; a USING alias adds only merged keys, while a whole alias hides inputs.
ownership: Owns scopes and new result records; merge(left,right) copies both input scopes while they remain available for key lookup. Occurrence names, using lists/sets, merged column vectors and qualifier views own copied strings.
failure: Table Error is caught and relocated at RangeVar; unknown/ambiguous keys, duplicate aliases/USING names, unsupported joins/namespaces and mixed conditions reject. Join-level errors use statement.begin because join AST has no location here; Frame/work/expression/JSON/allocation failures propagate.
cost: Each RangeVar repeats full catalog validation inside find_table plus a linear table scan and O(table width) nodes. NATURAL performs O(left width × right width) charged name pairs; USING adds repeated linear lookups and O((left+right width)×key count) uncharged membership searches. Nested joins copy accumulated scopes and can incur quadratic aggregate scope-copy work; this is no runtime join execution bound.

purpose: Derive a default select-list label from a column reference, cast or generic expression.
inputs_outputs: ColumnRef returns its final String field; casts strip nested casts to preserve an underlying column name, otherwise use the outer cast type name; other expressions return ?column?.
invariants: No scope lookup, alias resolution or semantic validation occurs. select uses an explicit target name when present, although this default expression is still evaluated by the value call.
ownership: Borrows AST and returns an owning name string copied from its fields or a fixed label.
failure: Malformed expected cast/column JSON can throw Json::exception; identifier can reject wrappers. String allocation can fail. Unsupported expressions are normally rejected before this helper.
cost: O(nested cast depth) traversal plus name-copy bytes and JSON lookups; no Frame/work charges. At most one recursive return into a column case after iterative cast stripping.
review_author: Codex binding source reviewer (inspection-v4-binding-v1)

purpose: Bind one ordinary SELECT body while preserving requested semantics, visible output order and separate filters.
inputs_outputs: Checks supported SELECT fields, builds FROM scope, appends Boolean WHERE predicate, then binds scalar targets or expands * / alias.* into outputs; absent targetList preserves nullary SELECT.
invariants: DISTINCT requires exactly one empty marker and means set; absent DISTINCT means bag. Set operations/LIMIT options and unrecognized clauses reject. FROM is bound before WHERE and targets. Wildcards use current visible names/order, ignore a scalar target alias per expansion rules and require an input qualifier even for zero-column tables. Unknown scalar outputs resolve to string.
ownership: Owns local scopes and result outputs, copying names but retaining expression IDs for wildcard entries. Scalar target binding can append fresh expressions; previous comma scope is moved into merge.
failure: Unsupported fields/clauses, DISTINCT ON, wildcard qualification/no FROM and expression/name/type failures produce binding rejection. Work/depth/expression/allocation/JSON failures discard all private outputs rather than return a prefix.
cost: FROM/expression costs plus O(expanded column count + output-name bytes); each wildcard output charges once. Repeated scalar references repeat lookup/append, and output_name is computed even when an explicit alias exists.

purpose: Dispatch the parsed SELECT and recognize the single supported whole-result EXISTS form.
inputs_outputs: Reads the parser-guaranteed first statement. Ordinary SELECT delegates to select; a sole EXISTS_SUBLINK target binds the inner SELECT and records wrapper mode/alias before moving out the complete result.
invariants: Non-SELECT statements reject. EXISTS outer body may contain only target, ordinary DISTINCT and default op/limitOption: no outer FROM/filter or extra targets. Inner select-list binding still diagnoses unsupported/name/type errors. Outer requested semantics and inner semantics are retained separately; this path does not produce a nullary CQ.
ownership: Borrows syntax until completion and transfers result_ ownership by move; local Binder has no returned AST references.
failure: unsupported_statement or unsupported wrapper clauses/DISTINCT ON reject; malformed AST wrappers produce invalid_ast/JSON failure. Any delegated binding failure destroys the private result.
cost: Constant wrapper-shape work and JSON lookups plus the complete select cost; final move transfers containers without copying the catalog/source payload.

anchor: SqlBindResult bind_sql(std::string_view source, const Catalog& catalog, const BindOptions& options) {

Parser contract errors, earlier allocation failures, other exception kinds and allocations while constructing diagnostics may escape; API is not noexcept.

anchor: SqlDiagnostic diagnostic_at(std::string code, std::string message, std::string_view source,
purpose: Create an owned SQL diagnostic and derive PostgreSQL-style source coordinates when an offset exists.
inputs_outputs: Owned code/message, borrowed valid UTF-8 source, and optional byte offset in; owned `SqlDiagnostic` out.
invariants: With an offset, coordinates are one-based; line advances at LF, column counts Unicode code points, and character position counts decoded code points. Without an offset, all coordinates stay absent.
ownership: Moves code/message into the result; source is borrowed only during coordinate calculation.
failure: Internal callers must supply an in-range offset into valid UTF-8; malformed UTF-8 uses a separate diagnostic path because character coordinates are undefined.
cost: O(offset) byte scan when located; O(1) coordinate work otherwise. No heap growth beyond owned strings/result.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Map libpg_query’s one-based character cursor position back to a source byte offset.
inputs_outputs: Valid UTF-8 source and signed PostgreSQL character position in; byte offset or `nullopt` out.
invariants: Positions <= 0 and positions beyond the end are absent; the position immediately after the last code point maps to `source.size()`.
ownership: Borrows source and returns a scalar offset; it does not retain a pointer.
failure: No exception is created for an unusable upstream position; callers retain a diagnostic with null offset.
cost: O(source bytes) scan, O(1) auxiliary state, no allocation.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

anchor: std::size_t statement_offset(const nlohmann::json& statement, const char* field)
purpose: Read an upstream RawStmt offset field while accommodating omitted zero-valued fields.
inputs_outputs: Borrowed statement JSON and field name in; nonnegative `size_t` offset out.
invariants: Missing field means zero. Present fields must be nonnegative integer JSON values; range checks against source are performed by `parse_sql`.
ownership: Borrows the AST node and field name; returns a scalar.
failure: Wrong type or negative value throws `parser_contract`, treating malformed upstream JSON as an invariant failure.
cost: One JSON object field lookup and scalar conversion; no traversal or output allocation on success.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Parse one SQL statement under the shared native parser/deparser gate while preserving the existing JSON result contract.
inputs_outputs: Original SQL bytes and ParseLimits produce owning SqlSyntax or an original-source SqlDiagnostic.
invariants: Existing UTF-8, NUL, byte/depth, PostgreSQL-version, single-statement, and range checks remain. JSON, protobuf parse, and protobuf deparse wrappers use parser_detail::mutex(); child factories are entered only after a prior parse wrapper returns.
ownership: The lock guard and ParseOwner span parse_sql including JSON conversion; ParseOwner frees its C result before the lock leaves scope. No libpg_query pointer escapes; returned SQL source/JSON use ordinary cold workspace.
failure: Existing syntax/resource/contract diagnostics remain. ParseOwner cleanup and lock release occur on return or exception; parser_contract and allocation/lock failures are not converted into aggregate diagnostics here.
cost: One shared std::mutex acquisition per parse, replacing the former local mutex with the common gate; upstream parser and JSON work remain cold serialized work.
review_author: Codex independent parser-gate review; byte-compared unchanged helpers and parent Debug/SAN receipts

purpose: Represent a half-open byte interval in the owned UTF-8 SQL source.
inputs_outputs: Two `size_t` offsets, `begin` and `end`, defaulting to zero; comparable as a value.
invariants: Parser-produced ranges satisfy begin <= end <= source.size(); the aggregate type itself does not enforce that relation. PostgreSQL AST locations remain byte offsets.
ownership: Owns only scalar offsets; no source buffer is retained.
failure: No constructor validation or failure path.
cost: Fixed-size value, O(1) copy/compare.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Carry an owned SQL diagnostic and optional source coordinates.
inputs_outputs: Code/message strings and optional byte, character, line, and column positions.
invariants: Coordinate conventions are documented: byte offset zero-based; PostgreSQL character position, line, and Unicode-code-point column one-based. Malformed UTF-8 may have only a byte offset.
ownership: Owns strings and scalar optionals; no parser-owned pointers.
failure: The record does not validate code or coordinate consistency; parser construction establishes it.
cost: Fixed scalar fields plus code/message string storage.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Own a parsed source, complete AST JSON, and one statement’s range.
inputs_outputs: UTF-8 source string, `nlohmann::json` AST, and half-open `SourceRange`.
invariants: A successful parser result represents exactly one nonempty statement; retaining source and untouched AST preserves byte locations. This is syntax only, not binding or support.
ownership: Owns every field, so it survives later parser calls and upstream thread cleanup.
failure: The aggregate itself permits arbitrary values; `parse_sql` validates producer results before returning it.
cost: Source and AST sizes grow with the full input/parse tree; copying this record copies owned state.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Expose source-byte and AST-nesting bounds for the parser wrapper.
inputs_outputs: `source_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB and `ast_depth` to 256; callers may pass other limits.
invariants: The wrapper also enforces the upstream C API `int` size bound. These are operational caps, not a total memory or wall-time guarantee.
ownership: Plain scalar options copied by value into `parse_sql`.
failure: No construction failure. A request beyond a configured bound becomes a diagnostic in the parser.
cost: Fixed-size value; enforcing limits requires scans/AST decode work at call time.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Expose the syntax-success/diagnostic result type and parser entry point.
inputs_outputs: `SqlParseResult` owns either alternative; `parse_sql` takes a borrowed source view plus defaulted `ParseLimits`.
invariants: A successful alternative means one statement parsed syntactically; it grants no semantic admission. Both result alternatives are independent of libpg_query storage.
ownership: Variant owns its selected payload; the function returns by value.
failure: Diagnostics represent declared input/resource rejection; unexpected upstream-contract failures may throw `Error`.
cost: Returning success transfers/moves owned source and AST; JSON decode and copy costs are paid before return.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Map a binding/normalization/recognition diagnostic into admission phase and status.
inputs_outputs: Mutable result plus owned binding diagnostic in; result phase/status/diagnostic updated.
invariants: `resource_limit` has precedence; syntax phase maps to syntax error; `unsupported_*` maps to unsupported semantics; other declared diagnostics map to semantic error. `invalid_ast` denotes an internal invariant failure and is thrown as `binding_contract`.
ownership: Moves phase and diagnostic into result; reads code before moving the diagnostic.
failure: The `invalid_ast` exception path is required to avoid reporting malformed internal AST as a user semantic rejection. Other failure paths return a structured diagnostic.
cost: Constant classification and moves, plus error-string handling on the invariant path. No query or catalog scan.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

anchor: AdmissionResult admit_normalized(NormalizedSql program, planner::RecognitionLimits limits, NormalizeLimits grounding_limits)
purpose: Ground legacy normalized v1 to v2 when needed, then report bounded structural admission.
inputs_outputs: `NormalizedSql` that callers must already have producer/reader validated, recognition limits, and optional host grounding limit in; owned status, program, witnesses, route, limits, and work out.
invariants: The API precondition is producer/reader-validated v1 or v2 input; implementation checks schema version and grounds v1 using stored parameters/limits plus the tighter explicit/stored work cap, but does not replay-validate v2 here. Recognition must complete before a class or route is returned. Contradictions retain actual structural classification and use `constant_empty`.
ownership: Program is passed by value and moved into the result; returned program and analysis own their data.
failure: Grounding diagnostics use `rejection`; invalid version/invariant throws `admission_contract`. Recognition exhaustion returns `resource_limit` without partial class. Completed cyclic/non-free-connex results retain diagnostics and their explicit statuses.
cost: Optional complete v1 grounding plus bounded GYO analysis; existing binding/normalization counts are reported, not rerun for v2. Recognition work is separately counted; no physical plan, runtime, allocator bytes, or SQL proof is produced.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

anchor: AdmissionResult admit_sql(std::string_view source, const Catalog& catalog, const AdmissionOptions& options)
purpose: Run the SQL binding, normalization, and structural admission pipeline.
inputs_outputs: Borrowed SQL, catalog, parameters and stage limits in; owned `AdmissionResult` out.
invariants: First frontend failure stops the pipeline. Successful binding preserves requested SQL semantics; successful normalization supplies the core used for GYO admission. This does not execute SQL or lower a physical plan.
ownership: Copies/owns intermediate binding and normalized program via stage APIs; final result owns normalized program and witnesses.
failure: Binding and normalization diagnostics are mapped through `rejection`; their internal invariant exceptions propagate. Recognition and contract errors follow `admit_normalized`.
cost: Parse and source/catalog validation, binder, normalization, and recognition costs are composed; result counters are abstract per-stage work, not time/memory. Parsing, catalog-copy/validation overhead is not a separate `AdmissionWork` field.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Return the stable text spelling for one admission status.
inputs_outputs: One `AdmissionStatus` enum value in; corresponding owned string out.
invariants: The switch covers all seven declared statuses. An out-of-range enum value is an internal contract error.
ownership: Returns string by value; no shared mutable storage.
failure: Unknown status throws `admission_contract`.
cost: Fixed case dispatch plus string result construction.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Name the seven complete admission outcomes.
inputs_outputs: Values: admitted, syntax/semantic/unsupported rejection, cyclic/non-free-connex shape, and resource limit.
invariants: A status is a frontend/structural result only; it does not mean a physical plan or maintained runtime exists.
ownership: Scoped enum scalar.
failure: No enum validation in the type. APIs reject an unknown cast value when converted to text.
cost: Fixed-size value.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Distinguish a structurally free-connex route from a proven constant-empty route.
inputs_outputs: `free_connex` or `constant_empty`.
invariants: Constant-empty still retains actual shape analysis; routes are only set on admitted results.
ownership: Scoped enum scalar.
failure: No enum validation in the type.

review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Bundle inputs and limits for source SQL admission.
inputs_outputs: Binding options, owned specialized SQL values, normalization limits, and planner recognition limits.
invariants: Binding parameter declarations and normalization values are distinct; stage limits are applied by their respective stages.
ownership: Owns the parameter vector and option values; APIs receive the record by const reference.
failure: No aggregate-level validation; each stage validates its own inputs.
cost: Fixed-size limit records plus parameter vector/value storage; work follows selected pipeline.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Report effective binding, normalization, and recognition limits.
inputs_outputs: Three limit structs in/out with the result.
invariants: The field names retain stage boundaries; a grounding host cap may tighten stored normalization limits for legacy v1.
ownership: Owns only scalar/optional limit values.
failure: No aggregate validation.

review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Report completed/attempted abstract work by stage.

ownership: Owns optional scalar counters.
failure: No arithmetic or validation occurs in the record.
cost: Fixed-size value.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Own one admission status, diagnostics, normalized program, structural witness, route, limits, and work.
inputs_outputs: Status defaults to semantic_error; phase, diagnostic, program, structure, and route are optional; limits/work are reported.
invariants: A rejected/incomplete request must not be presented as having a completed structural class/route; a successful result remains frontend/structure only.
ownership: Owns strings, normalized program, diagnostics, and structural analysis.
failure: The record does not enforce field correlations; `admit_sql`/`admit_normalized` establish them. Internal contract errors may escape rather than populate a result.
cost: Moves/copies potentially large normalized AST/CQ and GYO witness data; costs belong to the producing stages.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Declare SQL and normalized-artifact admission APIs and status serialization.
inputs_outputs: `admit_sql` accepts source/catalog/options; `admit_normalized` accepts an owned v1/v2 normalized program plus recognition/grounding caps; name conversion accepts an enum.
invariants: The API boundary documents frontend plus structural admission only. Normalized input must already be producer/reader validated; legacy v1 is grounded before classification.
ownership: Results and input artifact are value-owning; no parser-owned pointer crosses the API.
failure: Each function’s declared diagnostics/errors are defined by its implementation; declarations themselves do no validation.
cost: Calls can parse, copy, normalize, and recognize a complete query; resource cost is bounded by stage limits except no global memory/wall-time guarantee.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

anchor: void require(bool condition, const std::string& message)
purpose: Raise the catalog contract error when one validation condition is false.
inputs_outputs: Boolean condition and message in; no output.
invariants: Callers use this for declared catalog metadata constraints; it is not a data-query theorem or constraint scan.
ownership: Borrows the message on success; Error owns/copies message when thrown.
failure: False throws `Error("invalid_catalog", message)`; true returns normally.
cost: One callee branch, but callers prepare std::string messages first: literal conversion and dynamic concatenation can allocate on successful checks. Failure additionally constructs the owned Error/exception.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection); root clarified caller-side message allocation

anchor: void unique_name(std::set<std::string>& names, std::string_view name, const std::string& kind)

inputs_outputs: Mutable set, borrowed name, and kind label in; set gains an owned name on success.
invariants: Empty or duplicate names are rejected; callers choose scope-specific table/column/constraint sets.
ownership: The set owns copied strings; input views/label remain borrowed.
failure: Uses `require` for empty/duplicate cases, yielding `invalid_catalog`.

review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

anchor: std::set<ColumnId> column_set(const auto& table, const auto& columns)
purpose: Validate a key/statistic column list and return its set form.

invariants: Every id is in range and no id is repeated; empty sets are valid.
ownership: Reads table and sequence; returned set owns its nodes.
failure: Out-of-range/duplicate IDs throw `invalid_catalog`.
cost: For k listed columns, O(k log k) tree operations and O(k) node allocations.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Accept the two declared constraint trust states.
inputs_outputs: Constraint status enum in; no output.
invariants: Only enforced and untrusted are valid.

failure: Unknown enum values throw `invalid_catalog`.
cost: One constant-time comparison pair.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Validate fixed decimal precision and scale metadata.
inputs_outputs: Precision/scale pair in; no output.
invariants: Precision is 1..38 and scale is 0..precision.
ownership: Scalar input only.
failure: Invalid bounds throw `invalid_catalog`.

review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

anchor: Row project(const Row& row, const auto& columns)
purpose: Copy selected physical values into a key row for reference constraint checking.
inputs_outputs: Borrowed row plus column-ID sequence in; owning projected `Row` out.
invariants: Caller validates row shape and column ids first; order and repetition are taken from the sequence (catalog validation rejects repeated key ids).
ownership: Reads original values and copies each selected `Value`; returned vector and any string payloads own their copies.
failure: No local range checks; caller preconditions must hold or vector indexing would be invalid. Allocation/copy failures propagate.

anchor: bool decimal_fits(const Decimal& value, DecimalSpec specification)
purpose: Check exact decimal representability under a validated fixed precision/scale.
inputs_outputs: Decimal value and precision/scale in; Boolean result.
invariants: No rounding or truncation: fractional digits must fit scale and integer digits plus scale must fit precision.
ownership: Borrows Decimal while producing a temporary text representation.
failure: Invalid specification throws `invalid_catalog` via `valid_decimal_spec`; no semantic rejection is silently converted to false.
cost: Creates `value.to_string()` and scans digit positions, O(decimal text length) with one temporary string.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

anchor: template<class CatalogView> void validate_catalog_impl(const CatalogView& catalog)
purpose: Validate catalog metadata and cross-references for either public or program catalog view.
inputs_outputs: Borrowed catalog view in; no output.
invariants: Checks positive catalog/source versions; unique names; known scalar kinds; binary collation; decimal specs; constraint names and key column ids; distinct estimate column sets; hint columns/reason; foreign targets, arity/types, and enforced unique target-set requirement. Nullable declarations remain valid metadata.
ownership: Borrows catalog throughout; temporary ordered sets own duplicate-detection keys only.
failure: Declared invalid fields throw `invalid_catalog`; nonbinary collation yields `unsupported_collation`. Unknown type is translated from `type_name` Error to `invalid_catalog`; it is not swallowed.
cost: Full metadata traversal; ordered-set insertions allocate; cross-reference pass scans foreign keys and target unique declarations, rebuilding column sets during match checks. Cost grows with schema/constraint metadata, not database rows.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Expose metadata validation for the runtime catalog record.
inputs_outputs: Borrowed `Catalog` in; no output.
invariants: Delegates to the shared implementation; accepts nullable source metadata and validates constraints’ declarations only.
ownership: Borrows catalog; no mutation or retained state.
failure: Propagates `invalid_catalog` and `unsupported_collation` from validation.
cost: Full metadata traversal and temporary validation sets.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

purpose: Expose the same metadata contract for serialized/program catalog records.

review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

anchor: template<class CatalogView> void validate_constraints_impl(const CatalogView& catalog, const Database& database)
purpose: Validate database shape and all enforced unique/foreign-key declarations against a complete reference database.
inputs_outputs: Borrowed catalog and database in; no output.
invariants: Revalidates catalog; requires matching table count; validates every row before projecting ids. Only enforced constraints assert data properties; untrusted entries are skipped. Empty unique keys permit at most one row; empty FKs require a target row for each source row.
ownership: Borrows both inputs; temporary ordered `Relation` sets own projected key rows during each constraint check. Does not mutate database.
failure: Shape errors propagate from `validate_row`/catalog validation; duplicate unique or missing FK key throws `constraint_violation`.
cost: Intentionally full-scan reference checker: all rows/cells are validated, then each enforced constraint projects rows and performs ordered-set operations. O(database size × enforced key work, plus set comparison costs); projected rows/sets are copied and allocated. Indexed enforcement is a separate future optimization.
review_author: Codex (root-directed read-only inspection)

review_author: Codex IR type reviewer (inspection-v6-ir-types-v1)

purpose: Reports the declared semantics, backend assumptions, operation modes, and implementation status of a physical artifact.

invariants: Public mutable strings/vectors are descriptors, not proofs or enforced guarantees. Constructing a profile or PhysicalPlan does not install maintenance/cursors or certify runtime bounds; tree validation is an upper-bound check only.

review_author: Codex IR type reviewer (inspection-v6-ir-types-v1)

purpose: Holds an immutable lowered plan and exposes compiled descriptors, input adaptation, and result assembly.
inputs_outputs: Factory from_compiled exports a caller-owned DTO; accessors return const references/views to route, source/query/tree, validation/identity, descriptors, options/profile, work, and result layout. adapt_input filters/projects a row; assemble_result checks assignments and emits an ordered/repeated core-head tuple.
invariants: Validated lowering checks tree routes with validate_tree; constant routes use canonical empty trees and route-specific checks. from_compiled exports an already factory-produced CompiledProgram and copies its existing validation/profile without rerunning P02 or proving a new minimum. Tree routes retain checked upper evidence; constant routes record checked constant operators rather than CROWN-tree minimum proofs for their retained body. This class is not a maintained runtime/storage engine.
ownership: The handle is shared_ptr<const Data>; copy construction shares immutable Data. Ordinary exported strings/vectors/model fields are copied, but TupleLayout/Projection descriptors use AccountedLayout/AccountedProjection::descriptor and share their existing Data/control blocks, account, metadata, and projection source/target tokens. This can retain those metadata blocks after CompiledProgram destruction without retaining the whole native program graph or tuple/row arena.
failure: Moved-from access reports invalid_physical_plan; missing input port, malformed row/layout or incompatible assignments throw, nonmatching input guards return empty, and constant_false assembly throws empty_plan. The class has no public mutable Data constructor.
cost: Plan copy/move construction takes fixed handle work; copy/move assignment can additionally destroy the old destination Data and all final-owned payload in proportion to its size. from_compiled recursively copies ordinary payload proportional to strings/vectors/JSON, while descriptor handles add refcount operations without another native metadata control block. adapt_input pays typed row/adapter validation, guard scalar comparisons, projection and copied payload costs. assemble_result checks assignment tokens and equality instructions, pays the bytes examined by scalar comparisons, copies output scalars and validates/constructs the result tuple. Native-backed descriptors can allocate the output payload/control block under their retained account. Lowering work counters do not meter these calls or cap allocator bytes.
review_author: Codex IR type reviewer (inspection-v6-ir-types-v1); independent root/IR audit F1/F2 applied by root

purpose: Open a lazy table-row or key-bucket cursor with explicit lifetime fences.
inputs_outputs: live walks current rows; bucket_cursor resolves an index/key then walks only that bucket; index_keys walks distinct projected keys/degrees.
invariants: Native cursors require both live State and facade_alive, unchanged revision and a nonaborted journal-reader phase. Ordinary factories reject an exclusive active journal.
ownership: Factory owns fixed cursor metadata (account-funded on native route) but keeps only weak table ownership. Entries borrow; the enclosing runtime must supply any read lease.
failure: Factory can reject owner/index/key/grant/work/account/allocation state; next separately checks its lifetime fences before dereference.
cost: Startup allocates fixed cursor data; bucket startup additionally pays index/key lookup and scalar-byte comparison. Successful traversal avoids full result collection and payload copy/pin; reference bucket next_entry still adds ordered-ID lookup.
review_author: Codex scoped storage primitive reviewer, 2026-11-12; V58 root: narrow inventory/comment successor received; unchanged callable contracts retained, 2026-11-15

purpose: Create independent live storage with fresh backend/arena owners.
inputs_outputs: snapshot_copy preserves live logical tuple/index IDs, high-water counters/revision and concrete traversal order while rebinding internal links/iterators.
invariants: It rejects an active journal and copies neither external pins nor retired allocations/source action history. The copied population is a new baseline.
ownership: Native copy uses the original query account and shares immutable metadata but owns separately cloned rows/index storage.
failure: Allocation, work/cap/account or invalid-state failure discards the private incomplete copy; source logical state remains unchanged.
cost: Visits all live rows/indexes/keys/memberships and copies/rebinds their data; native copy clones deep values. Indexed copy borrows one finite aggregate operation allowance, never one new grant per table.

inputs_outputs: Budget/item/input limits/accepted InputPositions in; charges row fields/text/decimal and a source-name/tree-depth envelope, checking relevant count ceilings.

ownership: Borrows values/source/map; no copied row, map or source text; TupleValuesView assignment can retain an existing immutable tuple owner only.
failure: Checked multiply/budget overflow throws work; row/source/count limit throws limit; invalid variant can propagate bad_variant_access. No source/runtime publication.
cost: Charges1+8 per row field+4 per string byte+82 per decimal; optional source adds L*(12+8*bit_width(N)), with O(log N) contains only at configured position ceiling. Actual row iteration O(F), source-name lookup byte comparisons as needed.

purpose: Guard multiplication before reserving conservative replay units.

invariants: No multiplication wrap; budget.charge additionally bounds cumulative used.
ownership: Captures local Budget by reference; no backing retained beyond call.
failure: Overflow or cumulative exhaustion throws ImageFault::work before product charge.
cost: O(1) arithmetic, no dynamic storage.

purpose: Precharge only row-bearing physical events or window insertions.

ownership: Borrowed/retained existing view; no new native or ordinary row allocation.
failure: Column cap/work/accessor failures abort before caller validation/acceptance.
cost: Actual O(fields) iteration plus scalar getter/inline decimal work; text charge reads size only, later validator/copy performs text scans.

ownership: Borrows map and source-name bytes; lookup creates no key.
failure: Length/count/work failures are typed; accepted directory and progress unchanged.

invariants: No copy or implicit move duplicates ownership; GenerationOwner explicitly transfers via release/reset. Valid fd0 must be treated as owned.
ownership: Member fd_ owns one descriptor when>=0; no name/account ownership.
failure: Destructor/reset never throw; checked operational close failures are handled by FileIo after release.
cost: Fixed int storage, O(1) access/transfer and at most one cleanup close.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Borrow the currently owned descriptor number.
inputs_outputs: Const owner in; int out, possibly -1.
invariants: A returned number does not transfer ownership or retain the underlying descriptor; caller must not independently close an owned fd.
ownership: Borrow lasts only while owner remains live/unreset.
failure: No validity check or syscall.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Declare best-effort replacement/cleanup for unique descriptor ownership.
inputs_outputs: Distinct transferred fd or -1 in.
invariants: Old descriptor is closed once; same-fd reset is outside internal use. Use release before checked close when an error must be observed.
ownership: Adopts new fd, releases old ownership.
failure: noexcept and errno-preserving implementation; cannot unlink names or certify durable data.
cost: At most one raw close outside operation budgets.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Transfer descriptor ownership without closing.
inputs_outputs: Owned int out and member becomes -1.
invariants: Caller must immediately adopt or close result; current call sites pass it directly to checked close or another FileDescriptor reset.
ownership: Owner relinquishes all cleanup obligation for returned fd.
failure: noexcept; release itself cannot report or recover close failure.
cost: O(1), zero syscalls/allocation.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Carry per-operation syscall quota and publication knowledge.
inputs_outputs: Copied CheckpointFileLimits, monotone operations0 and publication not_published, stage dispatcher.
invariants: Limits/counters are mutable internal plumbing, not a public recovery capability. Publication transitions are maintained by call and publish_session_image. Reader uses the same dispatch with not_published state.
ownership: Owns only fixed limits/counters; call borrows every fd/name/buffer.
failure: Limit failure/returned errno are handled at real read/publication boundaries; no poison/reset framework is embedded.
cost: Fixed storage; operations counts admitted attempts, excluding raw descriptor cleanup and rejected-close raw cleanup.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Own one staged file-load lifecycle before receiving native restoration.
inputs_outputs: Constructor opens/preflights; memory_limit accessor supplies captured cap; read consumes remainder once.
invariants: Private directory/file ownership and original stat/prefix/size prevent caller substitution. Full checksum/program validation is deliberately deferred to caller after receiving buffer allocation.
ownership: Inline316-byte prefix/stat/counters plus two descriptor owners; no account is stored until read receives one.
failure: Construct/read failures unwind safely in actual wrappers. After read progress or fd release, reconstruct instead of reusing this loader; there is no retry/poison flag.
cost: Fixed preliminary state, one full receiving-account byte vector in read, then separate decoder/native allocations.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Expose the preliminary captured cap for receiving-account construction.
inputs_outputs: Decoded preamble memory_limit_ out.
invariants: Full checksum has not yet been verified. Caller may supply an explicit override and must still validate whole envelope/native binding before returning a session.
ownership: Returns a scalar, no account or authority.
failure: No throw or further validation.
cost: O(1), no file reread.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Keep file identity, read position prerequisites and cap together in the loader.
inputs_outputs: FileIo, directory_/file_, original stat, prefix_, size_ and memory_limit_.
invariants: Fields are private; constructor establishes regular bounded file and316 consumed bytes. Sequential fd position is implicit and not reset by failed read.
ownership: Descriptors own resources; prefix owns inline bytes; no borrowed path survives.
failure: Member RAII closes acquired fds on any later wrapper unwind; raw cleanup is not an admitted FileIo operation.
cost: Fixed per-loader storage; full image and restored graph are allocated only from explicit account.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Expose the private split between pure image validation and receiving materialization.
inputs_outputs: Session image/native checkpoint types and account-funded option access.
invariants: No public InputOptions/WindowOptions graph is introduced in binary restore; native codec creates original receiving-account values directly. These are local ownership rules.
ownership: No static owner or hidden memory account.
failure: No validation occurs merely by including this internal header.
cost: Compile-time boundary; actual metadata/native costs remain explicit.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Restrict adoption of freshly decoded native option structures to the internal codec path.
inputs_outputs: Friend access to private AccountedInputOptions and AccountedWindowOptions construction.
invariants: The helper is private-header plumbing, not an unforgeable runtime capability. Callers must supply already validated, correctly funded values; subsequent native controllers still admit semantics.
ownership: Transfers native option owners without exporting ordinary DTO graphs.
failure: Factory failures follow each owning constructor; no file/runtime publication occurs here.
cost: No generic conversion framework or second receiving account.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Move already receiver-funded input metadata into its immutable native shared owner.
inputs_outputs: Explicit account and AccountedInputOptions::Values rvalue in; AccountedInputOptions out.
invariants: Actual codec builds Values/map/text with the same account before calling. This helper does not independently check allocator equality or text/schema semantics.
ownership: Private constructor allocate_shared funds the control/Values object under account and moves nested nodes/text; no public InputOptions copy.
failure: Receiving allocation failure propagates; prior decoded Values remain RAII-owned during unwind. No live session has been installed.
cost: One account-funded shared control/value allocation plus member moves; nested map/text allocations already occurred during decoding.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Assemble native window options around an already funded table-id owner.

failure: Current body performs no throwing allocation/validation; prior table creation can fail before this call. Signature is not declared noexcept.
cost: Fixed assignments/shared-owner transfer; no new table buffer allocation in this body.

purpose: Carry one internal validation result and the exact borrowed bytes/limits needed by materialization.
inputs_outputs: Byte view, fixed InspectedSessionImage, copied state_limits and envelope limits.
invariants: This mutable aggregate has no private constructor/seal. Actual callers obtain it from validate_session_image, keep bytes immutable and do not edit metadata/limits; materialize does not rehash the envelope or inner runtime image.
ownership: Owns fixed metadata/limits only; bytes borrows external file/image storage through native restore.
failure: Forging/editing it violates the internal call contract; public inspection metadata is not a substitute for this call sequence.
cost: Fixed copying; no retained decoded graph or account.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Separate receiver-owned source/window checkpoint state from a temporary borrowed runtime blob.
inputs_outputs: SessionCheckpoint state plus runtime_bytes view.
invariants: materialize fills state native metadata and runtime manifest, while runtime_image.bytes remains empty; restore_funded receives runtime_bytes explicitly and performs actual native admission.
ownership: Native options/rows/maps own receiver-funded bytes; runtime_bytes aliases the unchanged outer image only until synchronous restore completes.
failure: Partial materialization failure destroys owned state; callers retain input buffer through restore. No partly restored session escapes.
cost: Owned metadata/row allocations plus one borrowed runtime span, avoiding a duplicate runtime-image buffer.
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Declare complete allocation-free envelope and nested-runtime validation before materialization.
inputs_outputs: Immutable bytes, native limits and image limits in; internal validation carrier out.
invariants: Checks full envelope SHA/structure/metadata, nested runtime inspection and consistency; reserves a conservative second-read work amount. Native program/source/window acceptance still follows.
ownership: Output borrows bytes and owns only fixed metadata/limits.
failure: ImageFailure before decoded output graph; caller must keep unchanged bytes and exact returned carrier for next phase.
cost: Envelope scans/SHA+nested image work+reserved second parse; fixed inspection allocations only (no heap graph).
review_author: astra_recovery_boundaries_human_review_v1: source/caller review, 2026-11-12

purpose: Declare receiving-account assembly using an unchanged prior validation.

ownership: All new native metadata uses supplied account; borrowed runtime bytes live through final restore.
failure: Account or pass-two validation failure releases private state. It does not publish a session, mutate input or mint another work/account grant.
cost: One materialization pass with metadata/row copying and option-control allocations; no extra whole runtime buffer.

invariants: The before decision controls execution; after-callback return is discarded. Open/create after-errors are normalized before acquisition; close still really releases the descriptor. Injected mutation errors can retain conservative unknown publication state.
ownership: Fixed owning scalar DTO. No file descriptor, error message, account or automatic restoration responsibility.
failure: Models selected syscall errno/partial transfer paths, not C++ new denial, system malloc failure, device durability or all process-crash behaviors.
cost: Fixed selection/clamping, plus successful entropy-byte overwrite when requested; real I/O and user callback work remain.
review_author: Codex remaining test-support semantic reviewer, 2026-11-12

purpose: Specify a nonthrowing private syscall hook with an explicit borrowed context.
inputs_outputs: Function pointer receives const event reference and void* context and returns a decision; tests pass a live Hook object address.
invariants: Callback must satisfy noexcept and avoid reentering the instrumented owner unexpectedly. Before/after notifications are synchronous on the caller thread; process-exit crash callbacks intentionally do not return.
ownership: Neither pointer owns its callback or context. Event/context borrows must end before caller destroys or clears the installation.
failure: A thrown exception crossing noexcept terminates; this is deliberately not an exception translation or retry layer.
cost: One indirect call for each installed notification; unset hook bypasses callbacks in the testing implementation.

purpose: Own a temporary test-directory pathname and schedule best-effort recursive cleanup.
inputs_outputs: Constructor calls mkdtemp with a mutable template, checks success, then copies the returned path; file builds owning child path strings.
invariants: Actual callers use an uncopied lexical Directory. Implicit copy duplicates the path/cleanup responsibility; the user destructor suppresses implicit move. This is test setup, not a durable directory owner protocol.
ownership: String owns pathname only, not an open descriptor. Destructor removes filesystem entries; sessions in enclosing fixtures die before the Directory.
failure: mkdtemp/check or subsequent string allocation can fail; allocation after creation can leave a directory. remove_all(error_code) ignores filesystem error reporting but is not an allocation-free/no-terminate OOM guarantee.
cost: One real directory creation, pathname copy, and teardown proportional to remaining directory contents; ordinary filesystem/string allocations lie outside native query-account accounting.
review_author: Codex remaining test-support semantic reviewer, 2026-11-12

purpose: Create the fixture's unique filesystem directory.

invariants: Template buffer remains live for the synchronous call and has a terminating NUL; no user pathname is interpreted.
ownership: On success the Directory string retains the path. Raw created directory precedes string ownership and is not guarded during failed string assignment.
failure: OS failure is asserted with runtime_error; ordinary allocation may throw after mkdir succeeded. Current callers create fixtures before injected failures.
cost: Fixed template preparation, one mkdtemp operation, and one ordinary pathname copy/allocation.

purpose: Attempt to remove this test directory and its remaining files on scope exit.
inputs_outputs: Calls filesystem::remove_all(name,error_code) and ignores the returned count and error code.
invariants: Use one uncopied lexical instance; copies would attempt cleanup of the same path. This is cleanup convenience rather than a durability or descriptor-release assertion.
ownership: Destroys filesystem entries named by an owned string; does not close arbitrary session descriptors itself.
failure: Reported filesystem errors are deliberately ignored. The destructor is implicitly noexcept, and general allocation failure is not guaranteed impossible by error_code.
cost: Filesystem traversal/deletion proportional to remaining entries; library/path allocation may occur.

Committed sequence/answer/snapshot/handles/root IDs and prior journal pins equal pre-state, then the same runtime retries the full batch at the same sequence and matches the clean oracle. First success must match oracle; caller separately requires failures at begin and all three stages and zero commit failures.
ownership: Each loop owns one runtime and an optional move-only PendingEpoch; prior shared journal pins and copied images remain caller-owned. After failure, cleanup and a same-owner full-batch retry occur before the next fresh trial.
failure: Only std::bad_alloc at replaced ordinary global new/new[] is injected. Account admission can precede the C++ new cut but no MemoryAccount cap denial is synthesized; raw malloc, aligned/nothrow overloads and syscalls are outside. Operation errors other than caught bad_alloc propagate.
cost: At most 8192 selected C++ new positions per direction, stopping at first successful full batch; each position rebuilds the tiny baseline and verifies several snapshot/event oracles. Not a performance, bytes, or CPU bound.
references: docs/prepared_epochs.md § Batch event and resource accounting

failure: expect_error checks exact busy/invalid_epoch codes; other allocation/runtime errors propagate. No allocation fault is injected.
cost: One stage, one snapshot and a fixed set of busy guards on a small runtime; no memory or CPU measurement.

purpose: Count one thread-local allocation-failure position and return malloc-backed storage for an admitted ordinary new call.
inputs_outputs: Requested byte count and fail_after enter; one selected failure throws std::bad_alloc, otherwise a non-null malloc result exits.
invariants: The position is checked before malloc; positive values decrement once, zero fails without calling malloc, and zero-byte requests ask malloc for one byte.
ownership: Successful replacement requests are backed by std::malloc and released by the matching replacement delete. The seam owns only thread-local fail_after; returned storage is caller-owned until its matching delete.
failure: A selected fail_after position throws std::bad_alloc at the replaced ordinary global new/new[] boundary; a real malloc null also throws. Raw malloc/realloc calls and operating-system calls are outside. Aligned and nothrow allocation overloads are not replaced. MemoryAccount allocations that pass account admission and reach ordinary ::operator new can be intercepted, but this suite does not lower memory_limit_bytes or inject MemoryFailure from an account limit.
cost: One fail-index branch and, for an admitted call, one malloc attempt. The index counts intercepted C++ allocation calls, not requested bytes, account charge, RSS, or CPU time.

inputs_outputs: Forwarded op and verify callbacks enter; each loop arms `remaining=i`, catches bad_alloc only, disarms, runs verify, and on failure reruns op then verify before incrementing.
invariants: The same runtime/session/report used by the caller remains across all positions and retries; the retry is unfaulted. First successful point requires at least one earlier failure. `Unexpected` is not selected by these call sites.

failure: For each index, arms the new seam around op, catches bad_alloc only, disarms before verify, and on a failed point runs op again with injection off. verify compares exact native owner facts/clock and retained report encoding. Non-bad_alloc exceptions disarm then propagate.

purpose: Count generation-hook calls and terminate at one configured before/after syscall observation.
inputs_outputs: A GenerationEvent's after flag and Hook counters in; updates count/order flags or exits the child with status 77.
invariants: Only before events increment count; crash matching uses the same ordinal and selected side of the syscall.

failure: The hook is noexcept and does not translate failures; _exit prevents child cleanup at the selected boundary.
cost: Constant work per observed generation event; it does not count syscalls from the other installed file hooks separately.

purpose: Install all four retirement syscall hooks and clear them together with RAII.

failure: Construction/destruction are test scaffolding; hook installation is not nested or thread-safe coordination beyond the probes' thread-local contract.

inputs_outputs: Action selects Saved setup; Hook counters observed around perform; Hook returned after scope.
invariants: A trace with an ordering violation cannot be used as the fault baseline.
ownership: Saved owns the restored QuerySession while tracing; Installed is destroyed before the Hook is returned.
failure: Fixture setup, operation, or ordering assertion propagates to main as an exception.

review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Inject before/after failures at every observed retirement syscall and exercise short I/O and retry limits.
inputs_outputs: Retire/resume fixture plus each baseline ordinal/side; checks selected state, descriptor count and a subsequent sink-aware restore.
invariants: Only ENOENT reported after an unlink can be accepted as already absent; short transfers must preserve ordering; repeated read EINTR ends at the configured root-operation cap.
ownership: Each iteration restores the file snapshot, owns a temporary session, releases it before descriptor checks, and uses a fresh Hook scope.
failure: Expected carriers are GenerationFailure, checkpoint FileFailure, journal FileFailure or sink Failure; the fixture separately verifies selected state/output after each case.
cost: Two actions times two sides for each measured syscall, plus one three-byte short-I/O case per action and one 30-operation recovery quota case; baseline size is observed, not hard-coded.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Exit a child before or after each measured retirement syscall and verify restart from the recorded files.
inputs_outputs: Action, syscall ordinal and side in; parent waits for exit 77, then checks selected native pair/output and sink-aware recovery.
invariants: Every tested point is an actual syscall boundary seen in the corresponding baseline trace; test scope is process exit, not power loss.
ownership: Child inherits the fixture state and performs the operation; parent retains its own fixture and explicitly validates it after waitpid.
failure: Fork/wait/status mismatches fail the test; child exceptions exit with a distinct status rather than being mistaken for the hook exit.
cost: Two actions times two sides for each baseline event; each parent verification reopens the bounded generation fixture.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Fault each intercepted C++ allocation during retirement and prove no allocation after intent publication.
inputs_outputs: A successful retire/resume yields a count; each position is failed in a fresh attempt and compared with saved file bytes and descriptor count.
invariants: The S04 seam counts replaced scalar/array, aligned and nothrow C++ new calls, not bytes or direct libc calls; resume count must match receiving-account successful allocation statistics.
ownership: Scope is nonnested and thread-local; each failed QuerySession owner is reset before lock checks; MemoryAccount lifetime follows the accounted owner.
failure: Each selected position must throw bad_alloc before mutating saved durable files; a one-byte-under replay heap cap must produce MemoryFailure.
cost: One measured operation per action plus one failure attempt per intercepted new position; heap peak and allocation-call count are separate quantities; successful retire is then denied further new calls at the intent link.
review_author: Luna Max
