invariants: Journal enable allocations equal account successful allocation deltas; persisted records retain reader bytes/records/header/permutation/source offsets; stale checkpoint cannot create a WAL or replace checkpoint.
ownership: Source owns input stream and session account; decoded views borrow account-funded journal decoder output only while the `Decoded` owner exists; saved checkpoint/log bytes are copies.
failure: Expected checkpoint fault is caught; allocation mismatch, wrong origin or stale file mutation fails.
cost: Two CSV records and two decoded journal input frames; one enable allocation sample and one stale restore/enable path.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Check source and decoder positions for all supported journaled stream encodings.
inputs_outputs: Two storage modes, eight shared profiles and optional seeded checkpoint row; journal records are decoded and checked for row, source offset and CSV permutation.
invariants: Persisted decoder bytes/record counts reflect each profile; CSV alone records header/permutation; stream progress physical and command sequence reaches 2.
ownership: Profile owns exact source bytes; QuerySession owns stream/journal; `frames` and decoded views borrow only within each iteration.
failure: Any missing profile position, field order, source value, or changed count fails.
cost: Two indexed modes times eight formats times two baseline-seed choices, at most two rows and records per source.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Exercise journal lifecycle states and reject semantic window errors before WAL admission.
inputs_outputs: Created, paused and stopped typed sessions plus a window command with invalid withdrawal label.
invariants: Created/paused sessions may enable and commit; stopped session leaves no WAL; invalid semantic command leaves only header record and does not poison recovery state.
ownership: Each Directory owns files; each session owns its writer lock until scope end.
failure: Stopped/state and invalid-window errors are checked by category; any WAL input append or recovery_required flag fails.
cost: Three lifecycle fixtures and one invalid-command fixture, each with at most one input.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Check paused drain uses the durable journal decision and predecision allocation failure preserves retryable input.
inputs_outputs: Fixture offers first input, pauses and drains; then commits a second prepared input with S04 failing at the next intercepted new call.
invariants: Drain advances journal command/native progress but does not expose output; predecision bad_alloc leaves committed sequence unchanged, session healthy and pending input frame present; retry commits once without duplicate input.
ownership: Fixture retains QuerySession and cached input across retry; S04 Scope ends before subsequent checks.
failure: Expected first fault is bad_alloc before the durable decision; missing retry/output or wrong record count fails.
cost: Two inputs; one paused drain, one injected allocation attempt, then one replayed commit retry.
review_author: Luna Max

anchor: int main(){try{for(const bool indexed:{false,true}){for(unsigned kind=0;kind<6;++kind)typed_case(indexed,kind);windows(indexed);for(const auto fifo:{WindowFifoPolicy::global,WindowFifoPolicy::per_relation})duplicate_expiration(indexed,fifo);}stream_and_resources();all_stream_formats();lifecycle();drain_and_retry();}catch(const std::exception& e){std::cerr<<e.what()<<'\n';return 1;}}
purpose: Run the journaled typed, window, stream-format, lifecycle and drain acceptance cases.
inputs_outputs: main executes two storage modes, six query kinds, both window FIFO policies, stream suites and lifecycle/retry checks.
invariants: This entry defines only bounded dispatch; the assertions and their limits are in the callees.
ownership: main owns ordering; fixtures own sessions/files/streams.
failure: Any standard exception prints diagnostic and returns 1.
cost: Two storage modes times six typed query kinds, two duplicate-expiration FIFO policies, eight stream formats, plus bounded lifecycle and drain suites.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Give each file test an isolated actual temporary directory and a simple path builder.
inputs_outputs: Default construction calls mkdtemp and stores its returned path; file(leaf) returns a joined string, defaulting to file.
invariants: The object owns one lexical directory name; tests place their destinations and .crown-r2- temporaries beneath it, and the fixture does not model namespace recovery.
ownership: The std::string is owned by the stack fixture. Destruction calls remove_all after nested file owners leave scope and ignores its error_code.
failure: A failed mkdtemp trips an assertion. Cleanup is best effort, so an error can leave test files behind without changing a production owner.
cost: One directory creation and a small path-string construction are bounded by this fixture; filesystem removal walks only this test directory and is not a production cleanup guarantee.
review_author: Luna Max

anchor: inline void put(const std::string& path,std::string_view bytes) {
purpose: Install raw bytes for malformed-prefix and external-change cases.
inputs_outputs: The helper accepts a pathname and borrowed byte span, opens binary/truncate mode, writes the span, and returns no value.
invariants: The caller-supplied bytes are the exact file preimage used by subsequent open/repair assertions; this helper does not construct a validated frame.
ownership: The stream is local and closes on return; the caller owns the path and source buffer for the duration of the write.
failure: The assert(out) checks stream state after write; with assertions disabled this helper would not report an output error separately.
cost: The test materializes its input buffers before this call and writes exactly bytes.size() bytes; stream buffering and kernel work are outside any memory-account claim.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Read actual file bytes back for exact-prefix and no-mutation comparisons.
inputs_outputs: A path is opened in binary mode and the iterator range is returned as an independently owned std::string.
invariants: Tests compare all returned bytes; unreadable and empty files both yield an empty string because the helper does not separately assert open success.
ownership: The input pathname is borrowed; the return string and local input stream have ordinary lexical lifetimes.
failure: Open/read failure is not represented as a distinct error result, so callers must use surrounding expected-byte assertions to catch most failures.
cost: The returned string grows with file size and copies the complete fixture file; these bytes are ordinary test allocations, separate from owner-account accounting.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Sample the process descriptor count around owner failures and closes.
inputs_outputs: It takes no argument and counts entries yielded by iterating /proc/self/fd.
invariants: The comparison is a test-local leak signal, not a stable global descriptor inventory; the iterator's own transient descriptor can participate in the count.
ownership: The directory iterator is scoped to the call and the returned integer outlives it; no owner descriptor is retained here.
failure: A missing /proc/self/fd or iterator error propagates as a filesystem exception rather than being translated into a test assertion.
cost: The helper walks entries proportional to visible descriptors and allocates implementation-dependent iterator state.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Count private R2 temporary-name entries left in one fixture directory.
inputs_outputs: The caller supplies a live Directory; the result counts entries whose native basename starts with .crown-r2-.
invariants: It measures names in this directory only and cannot distinguish live from orphaned temporary inodes or infer a successful destination publication.
ownership: The Directory remains caller-owned; each iterator entry is transient and only the count escapes.
failure: Filesystem enumeration errors propagate. A matching unrelated test file also increments the result because the predicate is prefix-only.
cost: One directory scan and filename-prefix checks scale with entries in this isolated directory; no contents are copied.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Create a deterministic fixed-width hash-shaped test value.
inputs_outputs: One character is repeated into every element of a value-initialized ar::Hash and returned by value.
invariants: The result is a synthetic identity/checksum fixture, not a digest of any frame or an authentication proof.
ownership: The fixed-size result is returned as a value and carries no reference to the input character.
failure: There is no data-dependent failure path; this helper does not validate that the repeated character is hexadecimal.
cost: Work and storage are fixed by ar::Hash width; it performs no frame hashing and creates no dynamic byte copy.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Wrap integer scalars in the runtime cell representation used by fixture rows.
inputs_outputs: An int64_t becomes a storage::ScalarView returned through the Cell alias.
invariants: This constructs the nullable/runtime test value view expected by the SQL aggregate fixture; it is not a serialized cell image.
ownership: The returned scalar view is a value object; there is no heap-owned row or alias to a temporary buffer.
failure: The helper has no explicit validation or catch layer; conversion follows the scalar constructor contract.
cost: A single fixed-size scalar wrapper is formed; this helper does not allocate a tuple or charge a frame buffer.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Build a genuine bound SQL aggregate, selected native tree, and matching WAL/sink headers for file tests.
inputs_outputs: Default construction creates a 128 MiB MemoryAccount, binds the fixed query against catalog r(g,x), selects a minimum tree, admits capture-enabled runtime state, then fills query/descriptor/header identities.
invariants: The descriptor comes from the binder and selected actual tree; tests do not synthesize descriptor metadata. Capture is enabled so fixture commits yield complete before/after output frames.
ownership: The Schema stack object owns the receiving account, admitted descriptor/runtime and header values. Packets borrows it only while constructing retained Frame vectors.
failure: Binder choice, planner tree selection and admission are assertion-guarded in this fixture; allocation or runtime exceptions propagate to the test process.
cost: The account cap is 128 MiB, not a claim that setup consumes that amount. Binding, tree selection and runtime admission perform real native allocations charged to that account.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Encode the fixed WAL/sink scenarios from genuine runtime output and transport records.
inputs_outputs: A mutable Schema supplies account, program and headers; construction produces seven WAL frames and three sink frames with fixed sequence values in their bodies.
invariants: The first sink epoch is derived from a committed native batch. The middle WAL Reject only gives the file cursor a transport disposition; it does not validate semantic replay of that rejected input.
ownership: The constructor borrows Schema during encoding and commit preparation; finished Frames become owned by this Packets object.
failure: Assertions require one output from the nullable-key commit and successful fixture binding upstream; encode and account-denial exceptions are not hidden.
cost: It prepares two tiny runtime batches and encodes ten frames. Row/frame buffers are real native account allocations, unlike the fault hook's fixed observation array.
review_author: Luna Max

anchor: [[nodiscard]] static std::string prefix(const std::vector<ar::Frame>& frames,std::size_t count) {
purpose: Materialize an exact concatenation of the first N encoded fixture frames.
inputs_outputs: The method borrows a frame vector and count, then returns a new string containing frames[0..count) bytes.
invariants: No header or boundary validation is performed, and the caller must provide count <= frames.size(); callers use known fixture counts.
ownership: Frame storage remains caller-owned while each Frame::bytes() view is appended; the result string owns its copied bytes.
failure: An invalid count can index out of bounds, while string growth can propagate allocation failure; neither condition is translated here.
cost: The loop performs count appends and copies the sum of those frame sizes into one additional ordinary test string.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Assert that an operation exits by throwing some standard exception.
inputs_outputs: A callable is invoked once; the helper marks a caught std::exception as refusal and asserts that one occurred.
invariants: It deliberately does not distinguish FileFailure, ImageFailure, bad_alloc, or another standard exception; tests needing a category assert that separately.
ownership: The action closure and referenced owners remain with the caller for the synchronous invocation.
failure: A non-standard exception escapes, and assertions disabled would remove the helper's refusal check.
cost: One call and a boolean are added; exception construction/unwinding costs depend on the selected failing path and are not a cost measurement.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Recompute both protected checksums after a deliberate hostile-frame mutation.
inputs_outputs: A mutable byte string is hashed from frame_header_size for the body, then the body digest and protected prefix digest are written at fixed offsets.
invariants: The helper assumes a complete frame large enough for both offsets; it makes test bytes checksum-consistent but does not make their kind, sequence or schema valid.
ownership: The caller owns the modified std::string; hash results are fixed values and are not retained by the helper.
failure: There is no frame-length guard, so callers must pass a valid-size test frame; malformed contents are intentionally left for parser checks.
cost: Two SHA-256 passes process body/prefix data; no second frame string is allocated inside this helper.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Hold the immutable frame sequence shared by behavioral and syscall-fault cases.
inputs_outputs: Construction fills wal with a header, three Inputs, one Commit, one Reject and another Commit; sink holds its header and two complete epochs.
invariants: The packet set includes a real nullable-key change, a transport-only Reject fixture, and a real empty no-op epoch. The Reject is not an independent native replay semantics proof.
ownership: The vectors own their Frame objects for the fixture lifetime; encoding uses the Schema account. Helper methods only borrow these vectors during calls.
failure: Frame encoding/runtime preparation failures propagate; prefix assumes a valid requested count and does not bounds-check it.
cost: The retained frame set is finite and small, but its encoded buffers and runtime commit rows are native account allocations; prefix strings add explicit byte copies.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Describe one before/after observation delivered by the R2 test-only syscall hook.
inputs_outputs: The event carries stage, phase, operation ordinal, original requested count, returned result and native errno.
invariants: Requested is the original call size rather than the hook-clamped transfer size; after-events report actual call result or injected error metadata.
ownership: Events are passed by const reference only during a callback; the hook owns any copied observation it chooses to retain.
failure: The type performs no I/O or error handling, and a consumer can truncate its own trace without changing the file owner's operation count.
cost: The event is a fixed aggregate with no dynamic storage; hook-side trace arrays are separate test-owned memory.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Set deterministic pre-call errors, post-call errors, transfer caps, or zero entropy in the file probe.
inputs_outputs: A default decision requests unlimited transfer and no errors; a test callback may set either errno phase, a maximum count or entropy replacement.
invariants: The probe is compiled only for the testing seam, and its transfer cap changes actual POSIX call size without replacing the filesystem.
ownership: The value is returned by the hook for one event; set_file_hook separately borrows a thread-local function/context pair until replaced.
failure: An error-before decision skips most actual calls; an error-after decision reports failure after the operation, with acquisition stages normalized before open to avoid leaking FDs.
cost: The decision is a small fixed value; it does not count or inject C++ allocations and creates no syscall queue.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Exercise actual create, append, duplicate verification, move, close and reopen for a linked WAL/sink pair.
inputs_outputs: The function borrows fixture frames and schema, creates files in a stack Directory, appends two WAL commits plus two sink epochs, then checks prefixes and reopened byte streams.
invariants: The WAL retains transport W/I/C frontiers, including the synthetic Reject; sink duplicates return false only after byte comparison. Moving an owner invalidates the source; owner-level unlock/FD lifetime ends at close/destruction.
ownership: The two File owners keep their locks and receiving-account metadata for the function scope; frames remain owned by Packets and Directory outlives both owners.
failure: S04 denial is expected only for initial sink append scratch funding; the empty-receiver owners are not mistaken for native semantic replay or coordinator publication.
cost: It performs a fixed seven-record WAL and three-record sink round trip with one ordinary-new denial and two reopen scans. Frame bytes, metadata/index and scratch are actual receiver-account allocations; the test does not time them.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Check strict prefixes of representative next records and reject complete or authenticated-invalid records without rewriting them.
inputs_outputs: For a prior WAL prefix and sink header it varies the cut through one Commit/GroupEpoch, tests bytewise mutations and three resealed envelope mutations, then verifies a duplicate through a torn suffix.
invariants: Repair is called explicitly by the test after open; it does not perform the session-level native/source/sink validation that docs require before production repair.
ownership: Each WalFile/SinkFile owns its lock only until scope exit; path contents are reloaded through fixture streams, and the test reuses one directory leaf sequentially.
failure: Open rejects complete corrupt bytes and inconsistent kind/ordinal/length evidence. The finite mutation set is not an exhaustive proof over all hostile byte strings.
cost: Loops are bounded by one frame's encoded byte length plus three hand-built modes; each cut writes/copies a prefix, and open scans use actual receiving-account scratch and file metadata.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Exercise rebased transport ordinals, permitted increasing sink-I gaps, identity rejection and integer terminal frontiers.
inputs_outputs: The test makes a WAL header at C=10/I=17 and a sink at base C=10, appends I=18 and global epoch ordinal C=11, then tries falling metadata, relative ordinals, changed duplicate bytes and UINT64_MAX cases.
invariants: The increasing I gap is accepted at the sink prefix boundary but this rebased history does not itself write a Reject record. Terminal C/I maxima reject any impossible next record, and a wrong descriptor binding cannot create a destination.
ownership: The test owns two actual file owners at a time and closes the sink before the temp directory leaves scope; source Packets are only borrowed for one max-frontier refusal.
failure: Wrong generation/I, wrong relative C, different duplicate body, mismatched descriptor, or terminal suffix is rejected before an accepted append; these are selected cases, not every integer boundary combination.
cost: The scenario writes a fixed number of headers/epochs and one synthetic empty Input; its only stress is constant-width uint64 boundary handling, with receiver-account storage allocated by file owners.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Prove an owner's frozen schema and actual bytes gate append before file mutation.
inputs_outputs: The test supplies a genuine alien aggregate Frame, cross-kind WAL/sink Frames, and a moved-from Frame, then checks file bytes, owner health, records and operation counters.
invariants: Cached Frame info is not authority: owners inspect under their own program. A WAL transition thrown inside next.feed occurs before its work charge; this test asserts bytes and operations, not a work delta. SinkFile charges a successful generic inspect before later kind/order checks, so a parseable wrong-kind frame may still spend work. No native replay is tested.
ownership: The two owner locks are held for the checks; the original and moved Frame handles are stack values backed by account-funded encoded storage.
failure: Mismatched inputs are refused before append I/O and leave both owners reusable. The alien SQL is valid but structurally distinct; no claim is made about arbitrary codec corruption here.
cost: It creates two owners and a small set of frames/one row tuple; actual schema binding and output-frame allocations use the supplied account, while counter assertions cover only this test path.
review_author: Luna Max

anchor: template<class Factory> void receiving_limits(Factory factory,const std::string& path) {
purpose: Measure a valid open's receiving-account high-water and exact replacement-new count, then test allocation and file-limit cuts.
inputs_outputs: A factory opens the supplied path; the helper records S04 covered new calls and account peak bytes, injects bad_alloc at each measured allocation position, tests exact/one-byte-short account caps, and lowers work/operations/bytes/records one at a time.
invariants: File bytes and descriptor counts must recover after each allocation cut. S04 counts only its replaced C++ new forms; MemoryAccount requested bytes and POSIX activity are separate measures.
ownership: The caller supplies the factory/path and keeps the fixture file stable; each returned file owner is destroyed before post-failure account and FD assertions.
failure: Expected failures are bad_alloc for each injected cut and a standard exception for one-below limits; this test does not inject malloc, OS page pressure, or native runtime work.
cost: For N measured covered allocation sites, the helper invokes the factory N+9 times: one measurement, N injected cuts, exact/one-under account opens, stats and exact file-grant opens, and four single-limit reductions. Each attempt performs bounded real scan/metadata/index work; test sweeps are separate from ordinary append cost.
review_author: Luna Max; root scoped wording review

purpose: Check exact record/work/I/O limits, path/no-follow/create preservation and ownership across producer-account teardown.
inputs_outputs: It prepares full WAL/sink byte streams, calls receiving_limits, probes one-over record counts, unsafe names and symlink/open/create collisions, then appends through owners whose source Schema has left scope.
invariants: An owner freezes the admitted program into the receiving account and retains its file lock/FD independently of the producer runtime. Symlinks, existing destination bytes, and invalid path shapes are refused without replacement.
ownership: The stack Directory, receiver and producer account outlive the file owners that use them; optional owners are reset before FD/temp/account cleanup assertions.
failure: The selected invalid names, symlink and occupied target are refused; assertions cover only these path forms and one retained-owner lifetime, not all hostile namespace races.
cost: The test opens each three-record/two-epoch stream several times for exact cap checks and performs fixed descriptor and temporary scans; frame/index/schema copies are real receiver-account allocations.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Run the five deterministic behavioral groups over one schema and one shared immutable packet set.
inputs_outputs: It constructs one Schema and Packets, calls each helper once in fixed order, and writes a pass line only if all assertions survive.
invariants: The executable checks lower file primitives and fixture relationships; it does not exercise the native replay coordinator or certify power-loss durability.
ownership: Schema and Packets stay alive through every helper; each helper owns its own stack directory and scoped file owners.
failure: An uncaught exception or failed assertion terminates the test before the printed pass line; the print itself is not independent test evidence.
cost: The main sequence has five calls and no data-dependent loop of its own; costs come from the bounded helper cases and actual file-owner allocations.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Control and record one R2 file syscall fault scenario without replacing POSIX storage.
inputs_outputs: The stack hook stores at most 4096 fixed FileEvents and configures ordinal failure/crash, before/after phase, short transfers, zero entropy, repeated EINTR, cleanup errno, or post-stat allocation denial.
invariants: Only the before callback decision changes a syscall; the after callback can arm the S04 allocation counter or exit a child. A full trace silently stops recording without changing operation ordinals.
ownership: Installed borrows this Hook through the thread-local API; the hook must outlive the installation and is cleared at scope exit.
failure: Its noexcept callback must not throw; _exit(77) intentionally bypasses destructors only in forked crash children. Incorrect mode settings can cause assertions to fail rather than produce a file-level failure.
cost: The observation array is 4096 fixed stack events per Hook. It allocates no trace vector and does not replace or simulate filesystem state.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Install one borrowed syscall callback and clear it when the lexical guard exits.
inputs_outputs: Construction passes Hook::call and the Hook address to set_file_hook; destruction replaces both with null.
invariants: The underlying probe is thread-local and installations do not stack; nested guards would clear an outer installation prematurely.
ownership: The guard borrows the caller's Hook, so declaration order keeps it alive until after the guard destructor runs.
failure: No status is returned by set/clear; an incorrectly scoped hook could leave a dangling context, which callers avoid by lexical pairing.
cost: Two pointer assignments occur across guard construction/destruction; the guard itself owns no allocation or descriptor.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Name the lower-level file operation selected by the fault harness.
inputs_outputs: The five values route create/open, one append, explicit tail repair, or sink duplicate verification in prior and exercise.
invariants: Duplicate is deliberately absent for WAL in the matrix; repair input contains one partial next record, and the enum says nothing about coordinator semantics.
ownership: Values are copied into stack loops and helper arguments; no dynamic state is associated with a mode.
failure: Invalid enum values have no explicit default branch in the helpers and are outside the test's enumerated call sites.
cost: The enum is a fixed underlying test discriminator; scenario work is bounded by the small five-mode loop.
review_author: Luna Max

anchor: std::string prior(bool sink,Mode mode,const Packets& p) {
purpose: Build the exact initial file prefix for one fault-mode setup.
inputs_outputs: A sink selector, operation mode and packet bundle choose zero bytes for create, complete prior header/input/epoch records for other modes, or an additional 23-byte partial next frame for repair.
invariants: The returned prefix is fixture data only; it does not mutate the target path or infer what an interrupted syscall actually published.
ownership: Packets is borrowed while its frame views are appended into a new owned std::string returned to the caller.
failure: Mode-specific indexing assumes packet vectors contain the fixed frames made by Packets; there is no unknown-mode recovery branch.
cost: The function copies only the fixed selected prefix and optional 23-byte suffix; string storage is ordinary test memory, not receiver-account state.
review_author: Luna Max

anchor: void setup(bool sink,Mode mode,const std::string& path,const Packets& p) {
purpose: Reset one shared path to the chosen pre-operation byte image.
inputs_outputs: It removes any prior path and writes prior(...) unless the requested mode is create.
invariants: The test starts each injected attempt from known path bytes; temp names are separate entries and cleanup is inspected by callers.
ownership: Path and packet bundle are borrowed, while the fixture Directory remains owned by the enclosing scenario.
failure: Filesystem remove errors are not checked here; later creation/open assertions expose most setup failures but the helper does not return a status.
cost: One file unlink plus at most the selected prefix bytes written are done for each scenario reset; temporary directory entries are not recursively scanned here.
review_author: Luna Max

anchor: void exercise(bool sink,Mode mode,const std::string& path,Schema& s,const Packets& p,
purpose: Run one selected actual WalFile or SinkFile operation under the current hook and limits.
inputs_outputs: The function creates or opens with the supplied receiving account and headers; append uses the fixed next frame, repair calls repair_tail, duplicate calls sink verify, and only a successful path reaches checked close.
invariants: This is the actual lower file protocol only. No native preparation, publication, selected-root decision, source continuation, or coordinator repair authority is exercised.
ownership: The selected file owner is moved into the generic lambda by value and closed before path/account/schema/packets leave the caller's scope.
failure: The call propagates FileFailure and allocation errors unchanged to the test's caller; a failed operation may leave a durable destination or torn suffix that surviving reopens.
cost: One owner and its receiving-account metadata/scratch/index are created per call; append bytes are borrowed from Packets, not copied into a test-side queue.
review_author: Luna Max

anchor: void surviving(bool sink,Mode mode,const std::string& path,Schema& s,const Packets& p,
purpose: Classify actual bytes left after a failed call or child exit by reopening the lower file owner.
inputs_outputs: It accepts absent output only for create, otherwise checks exact known prefixes/full append bytes/fully repaired bytes and reopens WAL or sink to inspect bounded state.
invariants: A failed repair may leave the torn suffix or have removed it; a complete pending WAL Input must remain pending. This proves physical file state, not native semantic commit authority.
ownership: The function owns only its short-lived reopened file owner; caller retains path, account, schema and packet frames.
failure: Unexpected surviving bytes, bad checksum or invalid cursor fail an assertion or the open call; this helper does not attempt repair or cleanup.
cost: Each invocation reads the observed file into a test string and then scans it with a fresh receiving-account file owner; all prefixes are finite fixture frames.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Sweep syscall boundaries, operation quotas, selected EINTR/short-transfer behavior, and real process-exit cuts for both file owners.
inputs_outputs: It traces create/open/append/repair/duplicate modes, injects before each observed call and after supported actual effects, lowers the operation cap through each observed count, tests each listed retryable stage, clamps transfers, and forks at selected durability stages.
invariants: The child performs real POSIX calls and exits at hook boundaries; the parent checks bytes by reopen. Acquisition-after errors are normalized before open, and file-level crash cuts do not simulate power loss or establish future coordinator authority.
ownership: The stack Hook owns its fixed trace; each attempt owns fresh path state and a file owner. Forked child descriptors vanish at process exit, while parent Directory/account survive the sweep.
failure: Each injected operation failure must surface as FileFailure, release FD/account/temp state, and leave a prefix a new owner can validate. Only enumerated stages and durability events are covered.
cost: Iteration is finite by traced operation count and the 4096-event capacity: up to two failures per observed call, one pass per cap, selected EINTR/short-I/O passes, and one child per listed crash event. Real file metadata/index allocations occur on each fresh owner.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Establish that uncertain append failures poison a live owner and that a partial WAL suffix is repaired only by a reopened owner.
inputs_outputs: For WAL and sink it fails at four traced append boundaries on both phases, checks outcome and disabled getters/retries, then injects a short three-byte write followed by failure and reopens/repairs the WAL.
invariants: FileOutcome describes the lower file attempt; it does not grant native commit/retry authority. A new owner explicitly repairs the incomplete suffix while preserving the complete pending input.
ownership: The first owner is closed while poisoned; a second independently opened owner performs repair and append while the same path/account/schema stay live.
failure: Four selected boundaries are not a proof over every filesystem failure timing. The new owner must successfully scan before repair; no in-place retry is accepted on the poisoned one.
cost: The matrix has 16 bounded boundary/phase cases plus one short-write sequence; actual writes and scans use the fixed small frames.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Keep owners alive across injected repair/duplicate-verification failures to assert the poison latch directly.
inputs_outputs: The test covers WAL repair, sink repair and sink duplicate verification at each selected operation boundary before/after, then checks rejected getters and retries before close.
invariants: Reopen/survivor checks confirm lower-file bytes separately; a public caller must establish native/root/checkpoint/sink semantic preconditions before production repair.
ownership: Each owner remains in the lambda after failure until checked close, rather than relying only on destruction behavior or post-destruction file inspection.
failure: A failed repair/verify leaves the old owner unusable even when a syscall effect may have occurred; recovery authority comes only from a later validated open and caller decision.
cost: There are three mode families, each bounded by four or three observed operation points and two phases; extra assertions use fixed state/receipt values.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Cover post-prewrite-stat allocation denial, empty/short syscall outcomes, finite EINTR exhaustion, name collisions and explicit external mutation detection.
inputs_outputs: The function arms S04 denial after the first successful prewrite stat, checks no covered new call occurs through append, then exercises zero transfers, operation-capped repeated EINTR, 16 deterministic entropy collisions, cleanup-error reporting and changed-stamp refusal.
invariants: All append funding occurs before the allocation-denial point; this checks the existing path only. Filesystem errors are injected around real syscalls, and external writers violate the cooperative namespace contract.
ownership: A poisoned owner is closed and reopened before any explicit repair; persistent temporary names are checked or manually removed by the test. No test repair operation supplies native semantic validation.
failure: The EINTR loops stop at finite limits, including at most eight emergency cleanup attempts; entropy collision is fixed at 16 attempts. This does not claim unbounded retry, future coordinator authority, or crash/power-loss equivalence.
cost: Two ordinary appends have allocation denial after prewrite stat; remaining cases use fixed stage lists, a 30-operation cap, 16 entropy candidates, one short changed-file case and actual receiver-account metadata. S04 counts covered new calls, not all malloc/account activity.
review_author: Luna Max

purpose: Construct one native SQL fixture and run all four lower-file fault groups.
inputs_outputs: It creates Schema and Packets, then invokes syscall, append-poison, retained-repair/verify and exceptional-path helpers once each.

purpose: Collect the independent limits for one SQL aggregate session and its recovery work.
inputs_outputs: Caller-owned factory configuration in: admission/binder DTOs, checkpoint/capture/rebuild bounds, file/generation bounds and history/replay caps. Factories borrow const SessionLimits& only for their synchronous call.
invariants: replay_commands counts Input commands, not WAL frame ordinals. replay_codec_work cumulatively accounts Input decoding, canonical group output encoding, and full-output hash byte visits; WalFile's full scan has separate file limits. ReplayStatistics native/group/source counters are observations, not caps or CPU budgets. The original runtime Options remain caller supplied.
ownership: This public DTO can own ordinary vector/string parameter payloads. Data retains only its fixed LiveLimits projection; admission/rebuild/repair stay factory-local, while GenerationOwner owns its fixed generation limits. Original parameter identity comes from the genuine program or saved descriptor.
failure: Invalid values are rejected by the factory or the specific lower operation that consumes them; this record does not validate or normalize limits.
cost: Copying this caller DTO can allocate and scales with its binder payloads. Session factories do not copy the whole DTO: they copy seven fixed live groups/scalars. Existing cold descriptor rebinding can create a transient binder workspace; it is released before return.

purpose: Expose the four durable/session frontiers and whether the sole pending input or output spool exists.
inputs_outputs: A ready Session in; fixed scalar snapshot out: logged W, disposed I, native committed C, sink delivered D, selected generation, and pending/spool flags.
invariants: W is the last Input command sequence, not a WAL frame ordinal. I is AccountedInputProgress.sequence, C is the actual native runtime sequence, and D is the actual sink prefix sequence. pending means one owned Head; output_pending means one owned canonical Frame spool.
ownership: The result owns only scalar values and booleans; it does not retain Session, file, or runtime state.
failure: Session::state requires a ready owner and rejects poisoned, missing, or reopen-required members; this value is not an authority to edit any frontier.
cost: Fixed-size copy plus the owner-state reads; no source rows or WAL frames are scanned.

purpose: Report replayed Input/codec accounting and observed native/source work.
inputs_outputs: A replayed Session in; fixed counters for Input commands, codec work, native work, group work, and source IndexWork out.
invariants: commands counts replayed Inputs; codec_work counts the session-level Input decode, canonical output encoding, and full-output hash visits under SessionLimits. native_work, group_work, and source_work are accumulated observations from successful replayed Commits; they do not preempt native replay or change original per-command grants.
ownership: The value owns only counters; reading it does not expose the runtime or a mutable allowance.
failure: Counter overflow or codec/command limit exhaustion fails replay before the recovered Session is exposed.
cost: Fixed-size copy. Counter additions are constant work per successful committed replay epoch.

purpose: Present the synchronous, single-writer owner for genuine SQL aggregate state, durable input/output, and selected recovery root.
inputs_outputs: A receiving MemoryAccount and either the genuine SQL program/tree/options or a selected query root/path in; one move-only Session owner out. Factory limits are borrowed by const reference through return; their fixed live bounds are retained by value.
invariants: The owner controls the actual SqlAggregateRuntime, GenerationOwner, WalFile, SinkFile, input progress, at most one logged Head, and at most one committed output spool. Calls and borrows are serialized. W/I/C/D are distinct and may diverge only at the documented pending/reject/delivery boundaries.
ownership: AccountedUnique<Data> retains the receiving account and all session members. Session is noncopyable; lvalue-qualified views borrow its funded members and rvalue overloads are deleted. The caller may mutate/destroy its SessionLimits after return; no host DTO reference or owning binder-vector copy is retained.
failure: Input/resource preparation can leave one logged head pending. Uncertain file/root publication requires reopen/recovery. The public class does not add a generic retry engine, an undo framework, CLI, or R2 history retirement.
cost: Snapshot/status access is bounded by the selected native API; command work includes native prepare, canonical epoch preparation, and durable file operations. This interface claims no CPU or preemptive replay budget.

purpose: Own the sole decoded, logged Input and the pre-funded but unpublished source-position change.
inputs_outputs: DecodedInput plus InputPositions::Prepared in; one move-only Head retaining the complete frame/rows and position candidate out.
invariants: The candidate belongs to the live progress map but is not published until durable Commit or Reject. The input view borrows the decoded frame and remains valid while this Head is alive.
ownership: DecodedInput owns its complete frame and flat cells/replacements. Prepared owns a detached funded node for a new source, or borrows an existing map iterator; that existing node remains owned by the live progress map, which outlives Head.
failure: Construction/preparation failures occur before WAL mutation. Destroying an unpublished Head releases the input and candidate without advancing I or source positions.
cost: Owns one encoded Input plus its decoded view storage and the single source-position candidate; it is not a command queue.

purpose: Keep the genuine native batch token or one explicitly supported semantic Reject result private to the decision path.
inputs_outputs: A successful SqlAggregateRuntime::PreparedBatch token or an allowlisted RejectReason in; private preparation state out.
invariants: The token is the only native/source/group rollback authority and stays active through preview/output and durable decision append. A semantic error has already unwound the native preparation; resource and contract failures are not represented as Reject.
ownership: optional<PreparedBatch> owns the active move-only token until commit or RAII rollback; RejectReason is a fixed value.
failure: No generic exception-to-Reject conversion is permitted. Any failed pre-decision preparation destroys the token and leaves the logged Head available for retry.
cost: Fixed optional/value state plus the native token's already funded staging. No second journal or copied runtime state is created.

purpose: Define the one private ownership aggregate and its fail-stop readiness boundary.
inputs_outputs: Receiver account, fixed LiveLimits projection, real root/descriptor/runtime/progress and optional reader initialize the private owner; it later owns actual WAL/sink and one Head/spool.
invariants: Declaration order makes Head/spool and SinkFile/WalFile destruct before native runtime and root, while the account is destroyed last. ready rejects poison, missing/reopen-required files, non-ready native state, or absent root selection. No second live database or replay output queue is stored.
ownership: Data owns the actual root lock, WAL/sink locks, native runtime, progress map, pending input, and canonical output Frame under the receiver account. Only fixed operation/replay caps are retained; caller admission/binder payloads and other cold-only configuration are not copied or referenced.
failure: poisoned latches uncertain native publication, root selection, or full-file validation; callers cannot use normal accessors while latched. Destruction releases owners in the declared order.
cost: Fixed owner/control state plus live native tables, one pending Input, one output Frame, and per-file indexes; cost scales with the actual retained state, not a shadow copy.

purpose: Translate only the six named deterministic source/constraint/arithmetic errors into stable R2 Reject reasons.
inputs_outputs: Borrowed native Error code in; one of weight_mismatch, source_overflow, unique_violation, foreign_key_violation, aggregate_overflow, annotation_overflow, or empty out.
invariants: The mapping is an exact semantic allowlist. Memory/work/contract/underflow/internal-sequence failures and unlisted overflow names remain exceptions; no prefix or suffix rule broadens the set.
ownership: Borrows the error-code string_view and returns a fixed optional enum; it retains or allocates no message.
failure: Declared noexcept and has no fallback conversion. Adding a code requires proving that the native prepare rolled back and that recovery can reproduce the same deterministic decision.
cost: At most six short string comparisons; called only while translating a native preparation Error.

purpose: Validate next-command/source/reader progress and fund its unpublished progress node while taking ownership of one input.
inputs_outputs: Owned DecodedInput whose command sequence should be I+1 in; Head with the same input and prepared source-position candidate out.
invariants: Source names/counts and offsets obey checkpoint limits and strict per-source monotonicity; reader records advance by one, do not exceed command sequence, and reader bytes increase. These checks do not publish I or any source/reader position.
ownership: Moves the complete DecodedInput into Head. InputPositions::Prepared is tied to this progress map; its unpublished node is released if Head construction fails.
failure: Progress/limit violations reject before WAL append. No catch converts them to Reject and no progress is visible until publish.
cost: One source-position lookup/preparation when present, fixed reader checks, and a move of already encoded/decoded input storage.

purpose: Prepare the next physical epoch through the real atomic native token and recognize only allowlisted semantic rejection.
inputs_outputs: The one owned Head with command I+1 and current native epoch C in; active PreparedBatch preview authority or one RejectReason out.
invariants: The runtime batch uses C+1 for its physical sequence; Input command sequence is independent and can diverge after Reject. The native token owns all preparation rollback and remains private until the durable decision is appended.
ownership: Returned Prepared owns the actual move-only token. On an exception, native preparation RAII unwinds; the logged Head remains in Data.
failure: Only crown::api::Error with an exact code accepted by session_detail::semantic becomes Reject. All resource, work, contract, and other errors propagate with C/I/source progress unpublished.
cost: The original native/source/group grants and their actual batch work apply. This wrapper adds one token handoff and one short error-code lookup; it does not refill or replace native options.

purpose: Encode the full canonical group-value epoch bound to the selected generation, input command, physical C, and Input body identity.
inputs_outputs: Captured native Epoch and its current Head in; one owned encoded Frame containing changed/full-key group output out.
invariants: An uncaptured native preview is a transition error. Normal decision preparation uses the sink per-frame codec limit; replay additionally uses and charges the cumulative replay codec budget. Empty successful output still encodes a whole closing epoch.
ownership: The returned Frame owns its account-funded bytes; the Head and Epoch are borrowed only while encoding.
failure: Codec, work, output-cap, or allocation failure occurs before Commit append; the local PreparedBatch then rolls back and the logged Head remains pending.
cost: Codec work is linear in encoded data plus canonical complete-key ordering/comparisons; temporary key/index scratch and the retained Frame are bounded by codec/account limits. No CPU-time bound is implied.

purpose: Publish exactly the already durable Commit or Reject without constructing another rollback journal.
inputs_outputs: Private Prepared token/rejection, the Head's prepaid progress, and optional prebuilt output Frame in; native C when committed, I/source/reader progress, and optional spool updated by move/scalar operations.
invariants: The poison latch is set before native publication and cleared only after the token, prepared positions, progress, spool, and Head have been reconciled. Commit advances C and I; Reject advances I/source progress only. No new allocation is allowed after durable disposition.

Rebind the saved descriptor through the genuine path, read the selected opaque checkpoint, restore through the actual cold runtime factory, open/validate the actual sink, then replay the selected WAL. Require sink_floor<=D<=final C and D=C when a Head remains. Validate all files/root before repairing either incomplete tail, then validate again before return.

purpose: Fault every intercepted report-capture allocation position while preserving old reports and runtime state.
inputs_outputs: Calibrate N new attempts, then run points 0..N; each injected bad_alloc checks no partial output/current-byte change, retries capture, verifies the old and new values, checks stability, and validates account invariants.
invariants: N is measured per fixture and guarded by N<2048. Capture throws bad_alloc on the injected report path; this is not a no-throw capture API.
ownership: The original held report remains alive during the sweep; failed graph allocations are expected to roll back and the retry result is released each iteration.
failure: A predicate or unexpected exception escapes to main; expected bad_alloc is caught at the capture call.
cost: Two initial captures retain the old value and calibrate N. failure: Unexpected normalization or identity equality/difference fails.

failure: Expected update diagnostics are checked; post-error current state and earlier result readability are asserted.

failure: Writer/reader errors and any changed value/position fail assertions.
cost: Finite scalar/document fixtures and one codec roundtrip; ordinary JSON allocations are not measured.

review_author: Codex source reviewer; independent V40 frontend peer review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

failure: Unexpected row count/value fails.

failure: Caught exception is printed and returns nonzero.

failure: A zero or small budget limits enumeration; it does not mean the family is unsupported.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

ownership: The plan vector and each representative tree are owned by the result.
failure: Allocation/container/work limits may return a prefix with resource_limited=true.
cost: Storage scales with retained distinct signatures and trees; work_units counts reference transitions, not CPU.

purpose: Check q-hierarchical incidence conditions for the selected residual.

anchor: ResidualView make_terminal_view(const Query& original, const std::vector<std::size_t>& members, const std::vector<VariableSet>& scopes)

purpose: Create a terminal residual Query view and dense local-ID maps.

invariants: Selected occurrences preserve input order; variables are ordered by VariableSet; constants, ignored terms, contradiction, aliases, and present output order are copied through.

purpose: Produce a deterministic frozen residual-trace record for one Query.

invariants: It has no initial validate_query or limits. Each layer freezes unique variables and both eligible anchor conditions before greedy deletions; later deletions do not discover new ears within that layer. Terminal IDs are remapped only in terminal_view.
ownership: The returned trace owns copied vectors, sets, records, and terminal Query data; input Query is borrowed.
failure: Invalid internal indices propagate at()/vector errors; allocation failures propagate. The helper does not convert malformed queries to a status.
cost: For each round it builds incidence and pairwise q-hierarchical checks, examines ear/anchor pairs, then greedily removes from the frozen list. The helper has no internal size cap or work meter; finite callers supply their own fixtures.

ownership: Operands/results are values; policy is borrowed for the call.
failure: Unsupported operations are rejected by the dispatch path; policy errors propagate to execute.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Parse and run one line-oriented annotation request.

invariants: It accepts multiplicity, signed-integer, and decimal domains with operation-specific fields; it prints ok before its late input.fail check and does not reject trailing tokens.
ownership: The input stream is borrowed; parser temporaries and result are local.
failure: Only crown::Error is caught by main; malformed stream state and unknown operation/domain throw std::runtime_error, while std::stoull conversion failures throw std::invalid_argument or std::out_of_range and also escape.
cost: Parses one request and performs one policy operation; input length determines parsing work.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Run annotation requests from standard input and map policy errors to text.
inputs_outputs: Reads each line, calls execute, prints an error code for caught crown::Error, and returns a process status.
invariants: The catch covers crown::Error only; it does not catch parser runtime errors. The driver does not reject trailing tokens after a valid request.
ownership: Owns only line-local streams and strings.
failure: Only crown::Error is converted to an error line; other std::exception types may terminate through the runtime.
cost: Processes each input line once; no explicit line-count or time cap.

ownership: Callable is owned by this helper for the call; code is a borrowed string_view.
failure: Mismatched Error codes fail via check; no Error causes a runtime_error; unrelated exceptions propagate.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Check support accounting separately from signed payload updates.

invariants: Positive support count and signed payload are separate quantities; changing a payload does not imply a support-membership change.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

failure: A duplicate cursor tuple or wrong count fails through check; commit errors propagate.
cost: Folds five raw values into two tuple counts, stages both tuples at both native occurrences in one epoch (four stage calls), commits, runs full bag/factor comparison, and drains another cursor for the explicit count assertion.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

failure: Expected runtime_busy/invalid_cursor codes are checked; assertion mismatches throw runtime_error.
cost: Opens two readers, checks a write rejection while leased, retains one row, cancels readers separately, deletes a row, checks cursor rejection inside a pending epoch, then moves a cursor and runtime facade. The successful model mutations also run full oracle comparisons.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

failure: Overflow or comparison mismatch fails via model/check.
cost: Per backend, runs one unary and one nullary fixture with two count replacements each, then checks constant_true and constant_false routes. The exact counts include 2^53+1 and UINT64_MAX.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

failure: Assertion or differential mismatches fail through check; runtime API errors propagate unless asserted by a helper.
cost: Per invocation, performs six typed-bag updates and two decimal-row updates, then tests 96-node visible and hidden chains with 98 and 99 updates respectively. Each BagModel update reruns full assignment/factor/result comparisons; each chain is drained for its frame-count assertion.

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

review_author: Codex independent V40 source review; independent reviewer: Codex V40 oracle contract review; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

failure: Catches std::exception and returns 1.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review

failure: Checks reject backend mismatch, missing strata, detail truncation, and pending capture; assertions throw on any unexpected result.

The primary owner then receives one further insert and one prepared-but-rolled-back insert attempt before final assertions. Capture and estimate work is repeated for both backends; no wall-clock timing is measured.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Compare the historical P07 binding bytes with bounded C02 encoding.
inputs_outputs: Receives Catalog and Query, builds expected bytes, checks exact key/payload caps, a one-byte-short cap, and a nonzero prior payload allowance.
invariants: Successful bytes match exactly; the cap applies to cumulative logical payload admission and preserves prior usage.
ownership: Catalog/Query are borrowed; expected/actual strings and Budget are local.
failure: The bounded encoder signals byte_limit through its Failure; checks expose any over-admission.
cost: Encodes the catalog/query multiple times; work follows their names, constraints, terms, and bytes.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Check that a standalone native artifact owns the complete binding after its source scope ends.
inputs_outputs: Builds and lowers a typed catalog/query/tree inside a local source scope. While those values are alive it validates the original and compiled catalogs against valid and five malformed databases; after the source scope ends it compares retained native binding bytes and exact/one-under payload admission.
invariants: The artifact binding matches the frozen v2 encoding; exact caps pass and one-under payload cap stops before excess admitted bytes.
ownership: CompiledProgram outlives local Catalog/Query/Database construction; it must retain its compiled identity, not borrow their strings.
failure: Bad database mutations fail validation; bounded binding failures must report byte_limit.
cost: One lower and validation batch with several source mutations; byte counters describe logical admission, not heap or CPU.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Run core and native binding comparisons over representative catalog/query values.
inputs_outputs: Calls compare for multiple fixtures and native_binding for one standalone artifact.
invariants: The harness checks binding identity and validation, not ranking or runtime installation.
ownership: All cases are local; native_binding retains its result only across the inner source scope.
failure: Assertion exceptions fail the executable.
cost: A finite set of catalog/query encodes plus one native lowering/validation campaign.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Provide test-only mutations for selected Collector census rows and diagnostic flags.
inputs_outputs: Scans collector descriptors to collect physical-root indexes and the first detail index, checks for at least two roots and one detail descriptor, then seeds selected committed counters/metadata for cases 1–9. Cases 7–8 clear committed rows and set maximum input/no-op totals; case 9 duplicates a root descriptor.
invariants: Only private Collector state is changed; the seam synthesizes root/detail saturation, metadata protocol flags, denominator overflow and duplicate-root structure without replaying public commits.
ownership: Collector references are borrowed; values are written into the test owner state.
failure: The helper requires at least two physical roots and one detail descriptor before applying a case; an incompatible fixture fails that check.
cost: Scans the descriptor vector, allocates a root-index vector, records a detail index, and for cases 7–8 clears and rewrites all committed cells; its work is not just scalar assignments.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Route a State test fixture through the collector mutation seam and add the configuration-saturation case.
inputs_outputs: Calls CollectorTestAccess::change(state.collector_, test); only for test==10 it also sets state.configuration_saturated_ to true.
invariants: Cases 0–9 delegate to collector boundary edits; case 10 marks configuration saturation. No StateStore counter is set to its maximum and no memory-account saturation API is used.
ownership: State is borrowed and mutated in place; the delegated seam edits its private Collector, and case 10 writes the State configuration flag.
failure: The delegated CollectorTestAccess check fails if root/detail fixture strata are absent; otherwise the seam sets the requested test state.
cost: Delegates descriptor scanning, root-vector allocation and committed-cell edits; case 10 adds one configuration-flag write. No maximum-length update sequence is run.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Exercise census completeness, saturation, and ranking refusal paths.
inputs_outputs: Loops over test values 0–10 to classify eleven isolated collector states, including maximum-root, denominator-overflow, duplicate-root and configuration-saturation cases; test 7 also sends the exact maximum census through ranking. It then separately captures one actual Delta owner after the runtime probe seeds C01 report saturation.
invariants: Census facts are independent of sampled detail; a saturated denominator or root is unavailable, and a score-width stop does not become height fallback.
ownership: Test seams alter private owner counters only for designated boundary cases; Evidence and Results are immutable captured copies.
failure: Every case asserts its explicit stop/reason; no failed score publishes a partial Result.
cost: Eleven isolated synthetic collector states plus a separate actual-owner saturation capture; one maximum-root case reaches the wide-score/bit-stop ranking path. Descriptor and candidate work is fixture-bounded, not a huge commit run.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Verify public ranking contracts for actual captures, resource stops, and historical evidence.
inputs_outputs: Builds fixture owners, captures evidence, ranks retained candidates under depth/slot/height policies and finite caps, then checks pending/foreign/stale boundaries.
invariants: Exact denominator and numerator facts are checked from finite updates; failed score-bit assessment has no height fallback, while explicit height request works; reset does not rewrite old as-of evidence.
ownership: Evidence and Result own immutable account-backed snapshots; owner remains external and can advance independently.
failure: Pending or foreign capture is unavailable; resource failure publishes no partial winner; ordinary check failures throw.
cost: Finite counter updates include 90 R plus 5 each S/T in the root-depth case and separate policy/cap attempts; ranking iterates the retained 3-candidate family.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Check ranking facts for empty sources and zero-node constant routes.
inputs_outputs: Builds nullary/unary fixtures with empty and nonempty rows, captures zero-cardinality sources, then ranks under source-work and C02 processing limits.
invariants: Zero source rows/keys do not erase exact cardinality; zero-node true and false constants retain their Boolean results; a processing work stop is distinct from source evidence unavailability.
ownership: Captured Evidence is an as-of copy; candidate snapshots and Results retain their own handles.
failure: Zero C01 work can make source facts unavailable; zero C02 processing work returns work_limit, not a partial result.
cost: Four cardinality shapes plus two constant routes and several bounded rank calls; empty scans do not imply no capture/setup cost.

review_author: Codex; root V40 source/caller/peer receiving review
purpose: Sweep ordinary C++ new failure positions across normalized C02 ranking and standalone owner evidence capture.

purpose: Compare metadata construction against an algorithmically separate GYO acyclicity decision on a bounded exhaustive multiset corpus.

cost: The whole family and root orientations can be exponential. work/fragments/cells/output_trees are finite selected grants; metadata checking has separate limits. They do not bound allocator bytes, vector capacity, every primitive comparison/sort operation, or total CPU. No incremental maintenance or paper delay theorem is claimed.
